overview.text: Looking for a quick escape to a whole new world? This 2-day trip to Morocco from Gibraltar is the perfect blend of adventure, culture, and scenic beauty. In just two days, you’ll cross continents, ride camels by the beach, explore the blue alleys of Chefchaouen, and discover the ancient charm of Tangier—all with the ease of private transport and guided experiences.

Whether you’re based in Gibraltar or visiting the Costa del Sol, this private 2-day Morocco tour from Gibraltar makes the journey effortless. You’ll be picked up from La Línea de la Concepción —just steps from the Gibraltar border—and travel smoothly across the Strait of Gibraltar into the heart of Morocco. For those dreaming of a trip from Gibraltar to Morocco in 2 days , this is the perfect plan.

"We had an amazing 2-day adventure to Morocco from Gibraltar with Tangier Excursions! Everything was smooth, from crossing the border and ferry ride to the private car and local guides. Tangier was lively and full of charm, and Chefchaouen completely stole our hearts with its blue streets and relaxed vibe. The riad was beautiful, and the camel ride along the beach was such a fun touch. Highly recommend this tour if you want a real taste of Morocco in just two days!"

description.text: Your private 2-day trip to Morocco from Gibraltar begins early in the morning with a pick-up from La Línea de la Concepción , just outside the Gibraltar border. Sit back and relax as your private driver takes you along the southern coast of Spain to Tarifa , where you’ll board the ferry for Tangier.

Once in Tangier, your friendly Moroccan driver will welcome you at the port. The day begins with a visit to Cape Spartel , the point where the Atlantic Ocean and Mediterranean Sea meet. After soaking in the views, head to the nearby beach for a fun and peaceful camel ride along the shore.

From there, you’ll drive through the Rif Mountains to Chefchaouen —famous for its blue-painted buildings and serene atmosphere. A local guide will take you through the medina, sharing stories and hidden corners. You’ll spend the night in a beautifully restored Riad , enjoying Moroccan hospitality.
Overnight accommodation at Dar Laman, Dar Echchaouen, or similar including bed & breakfast.

After breakfast at your riad, you’ll return to Tangier . A local guide will lead you through the city’s Kasbah, Medina, and colorful souks , giving you insight into Moroccan culture, history, and daily life. You’ll have time for shopping or a final mint tea before your guide escorts you back to the port.

Board the ferry back to Tarifa, where your private driver will be waiting to take you back to La Línea de la Concepción , just minutes from Gibraltar. Your Gibraltar to Morocco in 2 Days journey ends with new memories, photos, and stories you’ll never forget.

Professional local tour guides for exploring Chefchaouen & Tangier
1-night accommodation in Dar Laman, Dar Echchaouen or similar including bed & breakfast.
A camel ride experience by the sandy beach of the Atlantic

body.text: EMILY R. NY - USA

Start your adventure with a private transfer from La Línea de la Concepción to Tarifa. After a short ferry ride to Tangier, you’ll meet your Moroccan driver and begin exploring. Enjoy the panoramic views at Cape Spartel, take a peaceful camel ride by the Atlantic beach, and continue into the Rif Mountains to reach the beautiful blue city of Chefchaouen . Stay overnight in a traditional riad. On Day 2, return to Tangier for a guided tour of the medina before heading back to Spain.
Meeting Point & Pick-up:
Your private driver will pick you up from the La Linea de la Concepcion area at 7:00 a.m. (just outside Gibraltar’s border on the Spanish side).
The exact time depends on your location.
Travel Documents:
A passport is required to enter Morocco
Most EU, UK, and US passport holders do not need a visa for short stays
Ensure your passport is valid for at least 6 months from your travel date
What to Bring:
Comfortable walking shoes (Chefchaouen has steep alleys)
Sunscreen, hat, and sunglasses (especially in summer)
Light jacket or layers (evenings can be cooler in the mountains)
Euros or Moroccan Dirhams (some small shops may not accept cards)
A power adapter if you plan to charge devices (Morocco uses type C & E plugs)
Travel Time Overview:
La Linea de la Concepcion to Tarifa: ~1 hour
Ferry from Tarifa to Tangier: ~1 hour
Tangier to Chefchaouen: ~2.5 hours
Chefchaouen to Tangier (Day 2): ~2.5 hours
Tangier to La Linea de la Concepcion (after ferry): ~1 hour
Not Suitable For:
People with limited mobility, as Chefchaouen and Tangier’s medinas involve walking and steps
Travelers who prefer fast-paced sightseeing; this tour is relaxed and immersive

faqs.question: Do I need a visa to visit Morocco from Gibraltar?

answer.text: No , most travelers, including those from the EU, UK, and USA, do not need a visa for short stays in Morocco. Just bring your passport with at least 6 months of validity.

faqs.question: Where does the tour start if I’m coming from Gibraltar?

answer.text: The tour starts at La Línea de la Concepción , just across the border from Gibraltar. Your private driver will meet you there and take you to Tarifa to catch the ferry to Morocco.

faqs.question: Are ferry tickets from Tarifa to Tangier included?

answer.text: Yes, round-trip fast ferry tickets between Tarifa (Spain) and Tangier Ville (Morocco) are included in the package. The crossing takes about 1 hour.

faqs.question: Will someone meet us in Morocco?

answer.text: Absolutely. A friendly and experienced local Moroccan driver will meet you at the port of Tangier. You’ll also have official local guides for exploring Tangier and Chefchaouen.

faqs.question: What places will we visit in Morocco during the 2-day trip?

answer.text: You’ll explore Tangier with a local guide, enjoy a camel ride by the Atlantic, and spend the night in Chefchaouen , the famous Blue City nestled in the Rif Mountains.

faqs.question: Is accommodation included?

answer.text: Yes, the tour includes 1-night accommodation in a charming Riad in Chefchaouen, with breakfast included .

faqs.question: Is the camel ride safe and optional?

answer.text: Yes, the camel ride is safe and led by experienced handlers . It’s a short, scenic ride by the beach near Tangier. If you prefer not to participate, you can enjoy the beach walk instead.

faqs.question: What should I pack for the 2-day trip to Morocco from Gibraltar?

answer.text: Bring a valid passport , comfortable shoes, light layers, sunscreen, sunglasses, and some euros or Moroccan dirhams for small purchases. Don’t forget a camera —Chefchaouen is extremely photogenic!

faqs.question: Can the trip be customized?

answer.text: Yes! We’re happy to tailor the itinerary to your needs. Let us know if you want to start from Marbella, Seville, or Gibraltar, or if you’d like to extend your time in Morocco.

faqs.question: Are meals included in the trip?

answer.text: Breakfast is included at your Riad. Lunch and dinner are not included, but your guide will recommend delicious and safe local restaurants.

Upon arrival in Tangier, your private driver will meet & greet you holding a signboard with your name on it before embarking on your 2 day Morocco tour from Spain. Have a nice drive through the Rif Mountains while enjoying the breathtaking views.

After enjoying the stunning views, you may want to have a camel ride experience by the sandy beach before making a visit to the Neolithic Hercules Caves. overview.text: Private 3 Day Morocco Tour from Gibraltar

Join us on a once-in-a-lifetime 3 day Morocco tour from Gibraltar , where Europe meets Africa most effortlessly. Just a short drive to Tarifa and a ferry ride across the Strait of Gibraltar, you will find yourself wandering through ancient kasbahs, riding camels by the Atlantic, exploring Morocco’s famous Blue City, and hiking through the breathtaking Akchour Valley.

This private 3-day Morocco tour from Gibraltar is the perfect way to experience Moroccan culture, landscapes, and traditions in just three days. With seamless transfers, professional guides, and authentic stays in Moroccan Riads, this itinerary is designed for travelers who want comfort, adventure, and discovery all in one trip. If you’re looking for the ideal trip from Gibraltar to Morocco in 3 days , this tour gives you a complete taste of the country’s charm.

description.text: Get to Tangier from Tarifa by ferry across the Strait of Gibraltar. Your English speaking private driver will meet with you at the port upon arrival holding a banner with your name on it. Drive through the Ville of Nouvelle, which is divided up into different international districts as it was constructed & ruled by 7 countries.

Your sightseeing tour of Tangier will take you to the Cap Spartel promontory, where the Mediterranean & the Atlantic seas converge. The view, from here, is stunning; then to the Hercules Caves along the Atlantic Coastline but we may include a time for camel ride experience by the sandy beach if you feel you like it.

Asilah is your next destination; you will surprisingly appreciate the immense beauty of this artistic town with its colorful streets that attract painters & artists from all over the world every year putting their artistic stamp on its walls. Asilah was built by the Portuguese with the thick walls & ramparts highlighting this fact, the view of the Medina is impressive.

You will then continue on the track to the fishing port of Larache with its harbor that plays an important role in the whole region. Larache has a rich history and the old town is surprisingly intact being settled by the Phoenicians in the 7th century and the site of Lixus witnesses these historical facts.

You will continue on the track along the Atlantic to Rabat that marks the final destination of the day. Your driver will assist you to your Riad in the Medina, where the staff members will warmly welcome you with mint tea & pastries.
Overnight accommodation in Riad Kalaa or similar – Bed & breakfast option

After having breakfast in your Riad, you will visit the Oudayas Kasbah overlooking Bou Regreg River, Sale & the Atlantic Ocean. This dramatic Kasbah goes back to the 10th century but was fully reconstructed by the Almohads in the 12th. The view from here is spectacular; the beautiful narrow streets with blue-washed paint, the traditional bakery, the oldest mosque, and the friendly people are the captivating features of this amazing attraction.

You will have a walk through the Souks of the ancient Medina leading you to the Hassan Tower, which is the landmark of Rabat. This monument meant to be the largest mosque in the Islamic World by the Almohad Sultan Yacoub el-Mansour as he was planning to move the capital to Rabat from Marrakech. However, unfortunately, he died after 3 years of continuous hard work on the project. Adjacent to this monument, the Mohammed V Mausoleum built with white marble and topped by a typical green tiled roof, green being the color of Islam.

Next, you will head to Meknes through the Roman site of Volubilis. You will appreciate the rich history that Morocco is known for and the varied culture that has emerged due to centuries of peaceful coexistence. Enjoy the typical Moroccan Andalusian architectures symbolized in the Bab Mansour, then through the Royal Palace to the Royal stable & granaries. In the late afternoon, you will continue on the track to Fes that marks the final destination of the day.
Overnight accommodation in Riad El Yacout or similar – Bed & breakfast option.

itinerary.title: GUIDED WALKING TOUR OF FES – CHEFCHAOUEN

description.text: After having breakfast in your Riad, your private tour guide will take you for a lifetime cultural experience of this ancient Medina. You will initially form an idea about the rich history of this car-free city that goes back to the 7th century while enjoying the panoramic view. Drive through the old ramparts with its many gates to the Mechaouar or Dar El-Makhzen including a short stop for pictures at the Royal Palace with its impressive seven bronze gates.

You will stretch your legs at the Mellah (Former Jewish Quarter) with its vibrant Souk, then to the labyrinth of the Medina (a UNESCO World Heritage Site) through the tanneries and to the Impressive el-Quarawiyyin Mosque (Oldest University in the Islamic World). Visit the famous el-Najjarine Square, fountain, caravanserai, and woodwork artists. Drive to the 16th century Potters’ Quarter before escorting you back to your Riad to pack for our next destination, which is Chefchaouen.
Overnight accommodation in Dar Echchaouen or Similar – Bed & breakfast option.

After having breakfast in your Riad, your tour guide will pick you up for a nice walking tour through the beautifully painted streets of Chefchaouen. You will see that the blue-hued color is the dominant aspect of this unique city. It’s easy to fall in love with its myriad of cobblestone streets and blue buildings offering an exceptional opportunity to take nice shots. Visit the Kasbah (fortress), which is at the heart of the Medina. It was constructed by Moulay Ali Ben Rachid El Alami in 1471 to help defend the area from potential attacks by the Portuguese.

You will keep meandering around the endless alleyways leading you to the Ras El-Ma where women do their daily laundry. You will get some nice views and fresh orange juice. After that, you will walk back to the Outta El-Hammam Square with its many lined-café shops (ideal to watch the passers-by while sipping a delicious mint tea). In the late afternoon, you will have time on your own to getting lost, once again, within its streets to get another taste before getting back to your Riad.
Overnight accommodation in Dar Echchaouen or similar – Bed & breakfast option.

You may opt for waking up early to getting unique photographs while appreciating the stillness of the whole area. After having breakfast, your driver will pick you up back to Tangier through the Rif Mountains. We can drop you off at the port of Tangier to travel back to Spain or any location of your convenience in Tangier.

description.text: Your journey begins early in the morning as you arrive in Tarifa around 8:00 a.m. to board the 9:00 a.m. ferry across the Strait of Gibraltar. In just one hour, Africa comes into view.

Upon arrival at Tangier Ville Port , you are warmly welcomed by your private tour guide , who will accompany you throughout your Moroccan adventure. Your first stop is Cape Spartel , where the Atlantic Ocean meets the Mediterranean Sea, a dramatic and symbolic gateway to Africa.

description.text: Next, enjoy a camel ride along the beach , a relaxing and memorable introduction to Morocco’s coastal charm. You then visit the legendary Hercules Caves , rich in myth and natural beauty.

In the afternoon, head into the heart of the city for a guided walking tour of Tangier’s Kasbah and Medina . Wander through narrow alleys, historic squares, and lively markets before settling into a charming riad in Tangier for the night.

description.text: Continue to Meknes , once the capital of Morocco. Here, you explore monumental gates, royal granaries, and historic squares that reflect the city’s imperial past.

Overnight accommodation at Riad Sayeda Al Hora, or similar including bed & breakfast.

By signing up for this popular Best Private Morocco tour 10 days / 9 nights , you will have the opportunity to get most of Morocco. The tour is purely cultural, private & affordable. Arrive at Casablanca International Airport or wherever in Morocco, we efficiently customize the tour itinerary to cover the highlighted destinations on the itinerary.

The best Private Morocco Tour covers the Imperial Cities , namely Rabat, Meknes, Fes & Marrakech along with the blue town of Chefchaouen , the Roman Ruins of Volubilis, Sahara Desert, valleys, canyons, Atlas Mountains, and much more. You will have an in-depth history of Morocco, its culture, lifestyle, political fluctuations. To sum it up all, this tour is fruitfully informative and culturally immersive.

description.text: Arrival at Mohamed V Casablanca International Airport where you will meet with your English speaking driver through his eyes you will explore what Morocco has to offer through this meticulous Best Private Morocco Tour Itinerary . Transfer from the airport to the hotel.
Overnight accommodation in Jnane Sherazade Riad or similar- with bed & breakfast option.

Please note that it does actually depend on the time of your arrival since if it’s early during the day, then we may adjust the itinerary by providing additional services within Casablanca with no extra fees like visiting the Impressive Hassan II Mosque, drive through the Ain Diab Corniche and visit the popular Ricks Café. However, if it’s late we will then schedule such activities for the next day.

After breakfast we will make a visit to the Hassan II Mosque, a massive edifice that dominates the skyline of Casablanca; its main foundations lie partly on land and partly in the sea. Then, head for Rabat, which has been operating as the administrative capital of Morocco since 1912. We will visit the Oudayas Kasbah , a fortification that was founded by the Almohad dynasty in the 12th century; then developed and expanded by Moulay Ismail in the 17th century.

We will meander through its beautiful winding streets. We resume our visit to the Mausoleum of Mohamed V, whose wisdom and leadership led Morocco to get its independence from the French in 1956, built in white marble and the wrought iron entryway is remarkably beautiful. Adjacent to the Mausoleum, a beautiful tower of Hassan that was meant to be the largest mosque in the world; however, after three years of hard work the Almohad leader died and therefore the whole project did not finish. Drive further north to the beautiful town of Chefchaouen.
Overnight accommodation in Dar Echchaouen or similar – Half board option (dinner & breakfast are included)

We will spend the full day wandering around the “Blue City” of Chefchaouen or Chaouen. It is nestled high in the gray Rif Mountains, built on a hillside, and unlike the rest of Moroccan cities; Chefchaouen was the last town to be occupied by the Spanish. The Medina of Chaouen (Old Town) even though it’s a bit tiny, but you find yourself within a live museum. Our walking tour will take us through the blue painted narrow alleyways to reach the focal point of the Medina, the Place Uta el-Hammam, nestled at the foot of powerful-looking hills. Cafes line at the Place, across which is the 15th century Grand Mosque. The Kasbah was built by Moulay Ali Ibn Rashid Al Alami in 1471 and was used, firstly, as an Arab stronghold against Berber resistance to prison during the Spanish era. Leave The Uta el-Hammam Square strolling through colorful and charming streets to the natural spring of Ras El Ma, where you can catch the panoramic view of the whole valley.

links.text: Moulay Ali Ibn Rashid Al Alami

description.text: Overnight accommodation in Dar Echchaouen or similar – bed & breakfast option.

After having breakfast in your hotel, we will head to Fes crossing the Rif Mountains and will spend the rest of the day exploring the oldest Imperial city and the spiritual capital of Morocco. Your professional tour guide will take you to a vantage point to enjoy the majestic panoramic view of the Old Medina of Fes. Visit the Royal Palace Gate, the Jewish Quarter (Mellah), the famous Al Qaraouine University (regarded as the oldest official university in the world) and the colorful Chouwara Tanneries (built in the 11th century). The guided day tour of Fes will also include a visit to the Moulay Idriss II Mausoleum, Attarine Museum, and the Nejjarine Fountain. In the evening, we will escort you back to your hotel or Riad.
Overnight accommodation in Riad El Yacout or similar – bed & breakfast option.

After having breakfast in your hotel/Riad, we head for the Sahara Desert via the lush Middle Atlas known for the UNESCO preserved cedar forest. A short break will be at the beautiful and clean town of Ifrane, continue to Midelt where we will have lunch before we cross the High Atlas Mountains, Ziz Gorge and a nice stop for photographing the panoramic view of the palm valley of Ziz. We resume our journey through Erfoud and after some time we reach the golden sand dunes of Erg Chebbi where we will BE welcomed by warm mint tea at the Auberge that is located at the feet of the sand dunes. Dinner will be served followed by a time of entertainment before culminating the day with a drink by the pool under the illuminating stars.
Overnight accommodation in Riad Madu or similar – Half board option (dinner & breakfast are included).

itinerary.label: Day 6
itinerary.title: EXPLORE THE DESERT AREA & CAMEL TREK

description.text: After breakfast, we will spend most of the day exploring the desert area including a thorough introduction into the traditional system of irrigation that is known as Khettaras or aqueducts. Then to the Village of Khamlia that is resided by black Africans who were brought as slaves from Sub-Saharan countries and they are known for the spiritual music of Gnawa they generously perform to their visitors. Continue on the track to the Tafilalet Oasis to visit one of its old Ksers or possibly the weekly traditional market. In the late afternoon, we drive back to the Auberge in the desert for our camel trek experience to the desert camp that is located in the heart of the Sahara Desert. You will be amazed by the prevalent silence while enjoying a nice dinner.
Half board option (dinner & breakfast)

itinerary.label: Day 7
itinerary.title: SAHARA DESERT – TODRA GORGES – DADES GORGES

description.text: Early wake up in the morning to attend the panoramic view of the sunrise over the dunes before getting back to the hotel by camel; taking a shower, we will head east through Jorf, Tinejdad, and Todra Gorges. The Gorges or Canyons are very spectacular and have been popular attractions to both the locals and tourists seeking fresh and cool air or mountain climbing. After lunch, we will resume our journey to the valley of Dades crossing the administrative city of Tinghir. Dinner and breakfast will be served at the hotel.
Overnight accommodation in our luxury Starry Desert Nights Camp or similar – Half Board option ( dinner & breakfast are included).

itinerary.label: Day 8
itinerary.title: DADES GORGES – SKOURA – AIT BENHADDOU – HIGH ATLAS – MARRAKECH

description.text: Today, we will drive through the famous road of one thousand Kasbahs including a short pause at the Valley of Roses known for its annual festival of roses. We will resume our journey to the Ouarzazate (Hollywood of Africa) famous for its Taorirt Kasbah that is located at the heart of the city and the Atlas Film Studios where many Hollywood Movies were shot such as Cleopatra, the Kingdom of Heaven and many others. Then, to the Ait Benhaddou built over a hill to stand as a watchful eye for the caravans traversing the Sahara from the High Atlas Mountains. Drive to Marrakech over the Tizi n’Tichka Pass (2260m) that we will reach in the late afternoon.
Overnight accommodation in Xaluca Dades or similar – Half Board option (dinner & breakfast are included).

At 09:30 am, you will meet with your professional English speaking tour guide whose knowledge about the most hidden features of Marrakech is outstanding. You will first embark for an interesting sightseeing tour around the Ville Nouvelle of Marrakech that was built by the French when Morocco was under the French rule from 1912 to 1956. You will include a visit to the exotic and botanical gardens of Majorelle that was initially created by Jacques Majorelle and was bought and expanded by Saint Laurent. After that, you will head to the Menara Gardens with its olive grove, pavilion, and lagoon.

Begin your walking tour at the impressive mosque of La Koutoubia that was built in the 12th century by the Almohads with its minaret dominating the horizons of the city. Continue on the track to the Saadian Tombs that was built by the Saadians in the 16th century, then to the beautiful Palace of the Bahia before meandering around the vibrant and traditional Souks (Markets) of Marrakech to end your day tour at the Square of Jemaa El Fna (focal point of Marrakech) in the late afternoon.
Overnight accommodation in Riad Ksar Anika or similar – bed & breakfast option.

itinerary.label: Day 10
itinerary.title: TRANSFER TO THE AIRPORT OF MARRAKECH

description.text: Transfer to the Menara International Airport and assist with luggage. End of service.

DAY1: ARRIVE IN CASABLANCA INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT

Arrival at Mohamed V Casablanca International Airport where you will meet with your English speaking driver through his eyes you will explore what Morocco has to offer through this meticulous Best Private Morocco Tour Itinerary . Transfer from the airport to the hotel.
Overnight accommodation in Jnane Sherazade Riad or similar- with bed & breakfast option.

Please note that it does actually depend on the time of your arrival since if it’s early during the day, then we may adjust the itinerary by providing additional services within Casablanca with no extra fees like visiting the Impressive Hassan II Mosque, drive through the Ain Diab Corniche and visit the popular Ricks Café. However, if it’s late we will then schedule such activities for the next day.
DAY2: CASABLANCA – RABAT – CHEFCHAOUEN

After breakfast we will make a visit to the Hassan II Mosque, a massive edifice that dominates the skyline of Casablanca; its main foundations lie partly on land and partly in the sea. Then, head for Rabat, which has been operating as the administrative capital of Morocco since 1912. We will visit the Oudayas Kasbah , a fortification that was founded by the Almohad dynasty in the 12th century; then developed and expanded by Moulay Ismail in the 17th century.

We will meander through its beautiful winding streets. We resume our visit to the Mausoleum of Mohamed V, whose wisdom and leadership led Morocco to get its independence from the French in 1956, built in white marble and the wrought iron entryway is remarkably beautiful. Adjacent to the Mausoleum, a beautiful tower of Hassan that was meant to be the largest mosque in the world; however, after three years of hard work the Almohad leader died and therefore the whole project did not finish. Drive further north to the beautiful town of Chefchaouen.
Overnight accommodation in Dar Echchaouen or similar – Half board option (dinner & breakfast are included)
DAY3: FULL DAY EXPLORING CHEFCHAOUEN

We will spend the full day wandering around the “Blue City” of Chefchaouen or Chaouen. It is nestled high in the gray Rif Mountains, built on a hillside, and unlike the rest of Moroccan cities; Chefchaouen was the last town to be occupied by the Spanish. The Medina of Chaouen (Old Town) even though it’s a bit tiny, but you find yourself within a live museum. Our walking tour will take us through the blue painted narrow alleyways to reach the focal point of the Medina, the Place Uta el-Hammam, nestled at the foot of powerful-looking hills. Cafes line at the Place, across which is the 15th century Grand Mosque. The Kasbah was built by Moulay Ali Ibn Rashid Al Alami in 1471 and was used, firstly, as an Arab stronghold against Berber resistance to prison during the Spanish era. Leave The Uta el-Hammam Square strolling through colorful and charming streets to the natural spring of Ras El Ma, where you can catch the panoramic view of the whole valley.

segments.text: Overnight accommodation in Dar Echchaouen or similar – bed & breakfast option.
DAY 4: CHEFCHAOUEN – GUIDED TOUR OF FES

After having breakfast in your hotel, we will head to Fes crossing the Rif Mountains and will spend the rest of the day exploring the oldest Imperial city and the spiritual capital of Morocco. Your professional tour guide will take you to a vantage point to enjoy the majestic panoramic view of the Old Medina of Fes. Visit the Royal Palace Gate, the Jewish Quarter (Mellah), the famous Al Qaraouine University (regarded as the oldest official university in the world) and the colorful Chouwara Tanneries (built in the 11th century). The guided day tour of Fes will also include a visit to the Moulay Idriss II Mausoleum, Attarine Museum, and the Nejjarine Fountain. In the evening, we will escort you back to your hotel or Riad.
Overnight accommodation in Riad El Yacout or similar – bed & breakfast option.
DAY5: FES – IFRANE – AZROU – MIDELT – DESERT

After having breakfast in your hotel/Riad, we head for the Sahara Desert via the lush Middle Atlas known for the UNESCO preserved cedar forest. A short break will be at the beautiful and clean town of Ifrane, continue to Midelt where we will have lunch before we cross the High Atlas Mountains, Ziz Gorge and a nice stop for photographing the panoramic view of the palm valley of Ziz. We resume our journey through Erfoud and after some time we reach the golden sand dunes of Erg Chebbi where we will BE welcomed by warm mint tea at the Auberge that is located at the feet of the sand dunes. Dinner will be served followed by a time of entertainment before culminating the day with a drink by the pool under the illuminating stars.
Overnight accommodation in Riad Madu or similar – Half board option (dinner & breakfast are included).
DAY6: EXPLORE THE DESERT AREA & CAMEL TREK

After breakfast, we will spend most of the day exploring the desert area including a thorough introduction into the traditional system of irrigation that is known as Khettaras or aqueducts. Then to the Village of Khamlia that is resided by black Africans who were brought as slaves from Sub-Saharan countries and they are known for the spiritual music of Gnawa they generously perform to their visitors. Continue on the track to the Tafilalet Oasis to visit one of its old Ksers or possibly the weekly traditional market. In the late afternoon, we drive back to the Auberge in the desert for our camel trek experience to the desert camp that is located in the heart of the Sahara Desert. You will be amazed by the prevalent silence while enjoying a nice dinner.
Half board option (dinner & breakfast)
DAY7: SAHARA DESERT – TODRA GORGES – DADES GORGES

Early wake up in the morning to attend the panoramic view of the sunrise over the dunes before getting back to the hotel by camel; taking a shower, we will head east through Jorf, Tinejdad, and Todra Gorges. The Gorges or Canyons are very spectacular and have been popular attractions to both the locals and tourists seeking fresh and cool air or mountain climbing. After lunch, we will resume our journey to the valley of Dades crossing the administrative city of Tinghir. Dinner and breakfast will be served at the hotel.
Overnight accommodation in our luxury Starry Desert Nights Camp or similar – Half Board option ( dinner & breakfast are included).
DAY8: DADES GORGES – SKOURA – AIT BENHADDOU – HIGH ATLAS – MARRAKECH

Today, we will drive through the famous road of one thousand Kasbahs including a short pause at the Valley of Roses known for its annual festival of roses. We will resume our journey to the Ouarzazate (Hollywood of Africa) famous for its Taorirt Kasbah that is located at the heart of the city and the Atlas Film Studios where many Hollywood Movies were shot such as Cleopatra, the Kingdom of Heaven and many others. Then, to the Ait Benhaddou built over a hill to stand as a watchful eye for the caravans traversing the Sahara from the High Atlas Mountains. Drive to Marrakech over the Tizi n’Tichka Pass (2260m) that we will reach in the late afternoon.
Overnight accommodation in Xaluca Dades or similar – Half Board option (dinner & breakfast are included).
DAY9: FULL DAY EXPLORING MARRAKECH

At 09:30 am, you will meet with your professional English speaking tour guide whose knowledge about the most hidden features of Marrakech is outstanding. You will first embark for an interesting sightseeing tour around the Ville Nouvelle of Marrakech that was built by the French when Morocco was under the French rule from 1912 to 1956. You will include a visit to the exotic and botanical gardens of Majorelle that was initially created by Jacques Majorelle and was bought and expanded by Saint Laurent. After that, you will head to the Menara Gardens with its olive grove, pavilion, and lagoon.

Begin your walking tour at the impressive mosque of La Koutoubia that was built in the 12th century by the Almohads with its minaret dominating the horizons of the city. Continue on the track to the Saadian Tombs that was built by the Saadians in the 16th century, then to the beautiful Palace of the Bahia before meandering around the vibrant and traditional Souks (Markets) of Marrakech to end your day tour at the Square of Jemaa El Fna (focal point of Marrakech) in the late afternoon.
Overnight accommodation in Riad Ksar Anika or similar – bed & breakfast option.
DAY10: TRANSFER TO THE AIRPORT OF MARRAKECH
Transfer to the Menara International Airport and assist with luggage. End of service.

Overnight accommodation in our luxury Starry Desert Nights Camp or similar – Half board option (dinner & breakfast are included).

Overnight accommodation in Dar Chamaa or similar – Half board option (dinner & breakfast are included).

description.text: Meet and greet upon arrival at the Menara International Airport of Marrakech, assist with customs before heading to the Medina. You will have a private guided tour of the ancient Medina of Marrakech that was founded by the Almoravid “Berber warrior” Youssef Ibn Tachfine in the 12th century. You tour guide will shed light on the historical background behind the foundation of Marrakech as a whole and how it has witnessed great transformation over time.

The walking tour will begin at the Koutoubia Mosque, which is the landmark of this beautiful pink city occupying the horizons to the extent that it can be seen from different locations. Stretch your legs by the neighboring lush garden before continuing on the track to the Saadian Tombs. It is in here, most of the Saadian Dynasty leaders & family members are buried (this dynasty ruled Morocco in the 15th century and was known for their victory in the famous battle of the “Three Kings”). You will be immediately amazed by the immense beauty of the Moorish architecture of the tombs with stucco-works, Zelij tiles, lanterns, and the beautiful garden centering the site.

Meander around the vibrant alleyways leading us to the Bahia Palace (Palace of the Favorite). This spacious palace was built by Ba Hmad who was the vizier of the late Sultan Moulay Abdelaziz in the late of the 19th century. He built this beautiful masterpiece for his wives & concubines. It was used as the main residential place for the French General Lyautey when Morocco was under the French Protectorate from 1912 to 1956. Continue on the track through the vibrant Souks before getting the Jemaa El-Fna, which the focal point of Marrakech.
Your tour guide will accompany you back to your Riad to have enough time for relaxation to prepare yourselves for the best trip to the desert from Marrakech.
Overnight accommodation in Riad Ksar Anika or similar – Bed & Breakfast option.

Early wake up in the morning & after breakfast, you meet your private English speaking driver who is going to take you for a lifetime journey down to the Sahara Desert. You will drive through the High Atlas Mountains where you will enjoy breathtaking views. Berber Villages built in adobe & stones along the edge of the mountains offer an excellent opportunity for nice photo shots. Your driver will include stops for pictures wherever an attraction gets into your eyes. You will drive through the Tizi n’Tichka Pass (2260 m), then to Telouet Village.

In this village, the history of the reasons behind its foundation, the Glaoui family, its commercial & political role in shaping the recent history of Morocco when the land was under the “Lords of the Atlas” is just inspiring. Even though the Telouet Kasbah is, most of it, sadly, crumbling but the feeling you get once you step foot within its tiny alleys is, somewhat, exceptional. You will continue on the track to the Ait Benhaddou Village (UNESCO Heritage World Site) that has been used as a backdrop for shooting numerous Hollywood Movies including Gladiator, Lawrence of Arabia, Kingdom of Heaven and many others. You will be spending a couple of hours exploring this incredible site with your tour guide.
After lunch, you will drive through Ouarzazate (Hollywood of Africa), then the palm valley of Draa before reaching our final destination of the day, Zagora.
Overnight accommodation in Riad Lamane or similar with Half Board option (Dinner & Breakfast are included).

After having breakfast in your Riad, your Marrakech desert trip further east to the magical Erg Chebbi sand dunes. This part of the desert marks the gateway to the Great Sahara covering around 55 square km. You will drive through the lush palm valley of Draa and include a short stop at the Nkob town known for its spectacular Kasbahs. You will drive through Alnif and Rissani before reaching the Sahara Desert of Erg Chebbi, which marks our final destination for today.
At the Riad in Merzouga, warm welcome with fresh mint tea by the staff members and then you can stretch your legs at the sand dunes up to watch the majestic view of the sunset.
Overnight accommodation in Riad Madu or similar with half board option (dinner & breakfast are included)

itinerary.label: Day 4
itinerary.title: EXPLORE THE DESERT AREA & CAMEL TREK

description.text: After breakfast in your Riad, you will have the day out exploring the desert area and its countless highlights. You will be initially introduced to the “Khettaras” (aqueducts), which is a traditional system of conveying water from underground to the surface based on digging a line of wells connecting them with a channel. You will continue on the track through Merzouga Village before reaching the Khamlia Village – Resided by Sub-Saharan Africans who we were brought as slaves & have been known for the Gnawa Music (spiritual music) performed to the visitors using metal castanets and drums.

You will explore the Tafilalet Oasis with its Ksars that go back to the 14th century and its Souks that take place 3 days a week. In the afternoon, you will drive back to the sand dunes where you will have a camel ride journey through the dunes that like an ocean before reaching the luxury desert camp. In here you are going to enjoy the breathtaking views of the pure sand, the prevalent tranquility, the illuminating stars and much more. After dinner, you will have a nice performance of musicians with drums before getting to bed for the next day.
Overnight accommodation in our Luxury Desert Starry Camp with half-board option (dinner & breakfast are included)

Early wake up in the morning to attend the impressive view of sunrise; you will enjoy your breakfast before continuing on the track to the Dades Valley. You will drive through Tinejdad and then to Todra Gorge that has attracted mountain climbers from all over the world and has been an excellent escape for the locals to enjoy the cool weather of the place. Stretch your legs and enjoy the majestic views before resuming our journey further west to the Dades Valley marking, therefore, the final destination of the day.
Overnight accommodation in Xaluca Dades – Half Board Option (dinner & breakfast are included)

itinerary.label: Day 6
itinerary.title: DADES VALLEY – VALLEY OF ROSES – SKOURA – MARRAKECH

description.text: After breakfast in your hotel, you will drive through the Valley of Roses. You will make a guided tour of the Amredil Kasbah in Skoura before heading further west to Marrakech through the impressive High Atlas Mountains. Arrive in Marrakech in the late afternoon and we will escort you to your Riad. In the evening, you may want to stretch your legs at the Jemaa El Fna Square, which is the focal point of this magical city.
Overnight accommodation in Riad Ksar Anika or similar – Bed & breakfast option.

itinerary.label: Day 7
itinerary.title: MARRAKECH SIGHTSEEING TOUR & TRANSFER TO THE AIRPORT

description.text: After breakfast in your Riad, it depends on your flight’s schedule as if you have time. Your driver will take you to the Menara Gardens before dropping you off at the Menara Airport. We will assist you with luggage before getting to customs. Your Marrakech Desert Trip comes to the end.

Experienced English speaking private driver throughout your journey.
6 nights’ accommodation as illustrated on the itinerary.

Camel trek experience along with the overnight stay in our luxurious desert camp.

All amenities that are mentioned in the detailed itinerary
Travel insurance, which is required in case of a medical emergency

overview.text: Why Would You Want to Book This Morocco Trip 15 Days/14 Nights?

You may be possibly thinking of taking a long flight to an exotic destination like Morocco and planning to make the most of your lifetime trip, then the Morocco Trip 15 days/14 nights is the one to vouch for. We have spent time and effort to carefully design this comprehensive tour based on firsthand experience aiming, therefore, to clear the ground for unique cultural immersions while enjoying the breathtaking views that Morocco has to offer.

This Morocco trip 15 days/14 nights covers three major geographical parts of this magical destination, you arrive at the heart of the economic capital of Morocco, then head further north while exploring Rabat, which is the UNESCO listed and the current administrative capital before continuing on the track to the charming city of Asilah. Tangier is also in the list and few people know how to taste the mystery of this city, get to the Andalusian and UNESCO Heritage World Site Medina of Tetouan before spending a full day meandering around the intricate streets of the blue-painted town of Chefchaouen.

highlights.text: Meet & Greet at the Airport of Casablanca
Visit the impressive Hassan II Mosque
Explore Oudayas Kasbah, Mohamed V Mausoleum, Hassan Tower in Rabat
Meander around the serene alleys of Asilah
Unveil the mystery of Tangier
Explore the intact Medina of Tetouan
Wander through the intricate streets of the blue-painted city of Chefchaouen
Camel trek & explore the desert area
Visit the canyons, Kasbah and Ksers
Have a guided tour around Marrakech “ Pearl of the South”

description.text: The alluring Meknes and Fes, former Imperial Capitals of Morocco cannot fail to haunt the souls of its visitors, be prepared to be taken back to Medieval Times. Cross the Middle Atlas Mountains, explore the Desert Area & Tafilalet Oasis before embarking on a lifetime journey in the Sahara Desert on a camel and spend the night under the stars in the heart of the desert. Visit the enchanting Kasbahs that are shrouded in mystery; however, our mission is to unveil to Moroccan history, culture, customs, traditions and much more.

Explore the Ait Benhaddou Kasbah that have been used as a backdrop for shooting numerous Hollywood Films including Lawrence of Arabia, Gladiator, Prince of Persia, and The Kingdom of Heaven and may others. The guided tour of Marrakech is another highlight that cannot be missed with its unique ambiance, culture and lifestyle.

Upon arrival at the Mohamed V International Airport of Casablanca, your English-speaking private driver/guide – through his eyes, you will discover what Morocco has to offers – will meet and greet you before assisting you with luggage to the well-maintained SUV. Drive to the city center of Casablanca where you will have a tour of the impressive Hassan II Mosque before heading to Rabat where we will spend our first night.

Please note that it does actually depend on the time of your arrival since if it’s early during the day, then we may adjust the itinerary by providing additional services within Casablanca with no extra fees like visiting the Impressive Hassan II Mosque, drive through the Ain Diab Corniche and visit the popular Ricks Café. However, if it’s late we will then schedule such activities for the next day.
Overnight accommodation in a comfortable hotel/Riad including bed & breakfast.

Begin your walking tour from the Oudayas Kasbah (small fortress) that was built initially by the Almoravid warriors to use as a base to organize attacks in Andalusia, then was rebuilt and expanded by the Almohads in the 12th century when the Sultan Yacoub El-Mansour (the Victorious) was planning to move the capital from Marrakech to Rabat.

Visit the impressive Hassan Tower, which forms a small portion of a great project of the largest mosque in the Islamic World; however, it did not come into existence because the Almohad Sultan passed away after three years of construction. Enjoy the breathtaking intricate motif designs within the white marble buildings of the late King Mohamed V Mausoleum.
Explore the best of Asilah

Continue on the track, after lunch, further north to the serene and tranquil Asilah with its whitewashed walls, which display an excellent range of paintings that have been skillfully stamped by international artists who are being invited annually to participate at the International Festival of Art. Enjoy the stunning views from the ramparts over the Atlantic Ocean before driving to Tangier, which is our final destination of the day.
Overnight accommodation in LaTangerina or similar – bed & breakfast option.

itinerary.label: Day 3
itinerary.title: TANGIER – TETOUAN - CHEFCHAOUEN- GUIDED TOUR OF CHEFCHAOUEN

description.text: After having breakfast in your Riad, spend the first half day exploring Tangier from the outside and inside covering the Cape Spartel where the Mediterranean and the Atlantic Ocean meet, and the pre-historic Hercules Caves before embarking on a nice Tangier guided walking tour (small fortress) that is panoramically perched uphill overlooking the vibrant Medina and Gibraltar.
Meander around the authentic Medina with its vibrant Souks (markets) that are organized into different sections before continuing on the track to the almost intact Medina of Tetouan.
EXPERIENCE THE BEST OF TETOUAN

Unlike most Medinas (old towns) of Morocco, the Medina of Tetouan remains smaller but has been almost untouched aside few buildings that were saved from dilapidation when it was listed by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site.

Tetouan was expanded by the expelled aristocratic families from Andalusia by the Spanish Reconquista, a fact that can be seen from the wide streets and big buildings that have marble fountains, carved ceilings, and groves planted with orange trees. Wander through its alleys, and vibrant small markets before continuing on the track to Chefchaouen via the Rif Mountains.
Overnight accommodation in Dar Echchaouen or similar – Half board option (dinner & breakfast are included)

After having breakfast in your Riad, you will spend the day exploring this magical town that is nestled at the feet of two mountains with the shape of “goat’s horns” after which Chefchaouen was named because in Tamazight Language “Chaouen” means “Horns”.

You will be captivated by the prevalent blue color with which it is painted; meander through the beautifully painted streets with its shutters and wrought iron windows to the natural spring of Ras El-Ma where you can spot women washing clothes and carpets, and most of the time boys play soccer nearby.
Your private tour guide will give you an insight into the history behind the foundation of Chefchaouen as a Kasbah (small fortress) to fight against the Portuguese invasion.

You will visit this Kasbah which is located at the very heart of the Old Medina before ending your guided walking tour at the famous Utta El-Hammam Square. You may want to have lunch at one of the small restaurants overlooking the Kasbah and Mosque while watching the passers-by.

In the late afternoon, the Medina of Chefchaouen gets vibrant with its small shops selling all kinds of stuff from fruits, vegetables, crafts, electronics, clothes, and much more. You may want to have another taste of this unique lifestyle on your own before you get back to your Riad.
Overnight accommodation in Dar Echchaouen or similar – bed & breakfast option.

After having breakfast in your Riad, you will be picked up by your private driver to continue on the track further south by crossing the spectacular Rif Mountains from where you get to the popular Roman Ruins of Volubilis. This archaeological site is located in the very heart of fertile land planted with olive trees and orchards at the feet of the Zerhoun Mountain. It reveals a rich history of the Romans that occupied the north of Morocco and therefore powerfully influenced the lifestyle of the Amazigh people.

The archaeological local tour guide will unveil the mystery of this site before continuing to Meknes, which is one of the most important cities in Morocco It is one of the four imperial capitals that witnessed its glory and golden age during the reign of the Alaouite Sultan Moulay Ismail in the 17th century.

Begin your tour of Meknes from the beautiful gate of Bab Al-Mansour (Victorious) that overlooks the Hedim Square, which Sultan Moulay Ismail used for army parades and exposition. Visit the Sultan’s Mausoleum with its exquisite geometric designs depicting a mix of Moroccan and Andalusian architectures. Drive through the walls of the Royal Palace to the popular granaries that are used for storing grains, and stables for looking after the famous 12,000 royal horses before taking the highway to Fes, which is our final destination today.
Overnight accommodation in Riad El Yacout or similar – bed & breakfast option.

After having breakfast in your Riad, you will have a fully guided & purely cultural day tour of Fes with a professional local tour guide whose knowledge about the history and lifestyle of the city is outstanding. Drive uphill to catch the panoramic view of Fes El-Bali (Old Medina), which is one of the most car-free urban centers in the world.

Stretch your legs by the Mellah (former Jewish Quarter) where you will get an insight into the Jewish Community that settled in Fes before moving to Israel in 1948. It’s possible to visit the synagogue and take nice shots by the bronze gates of the Royal Palace.

Embark on a guided walking tour of this magical Medina that has gained popularity worldwide due to the exotic experience it offers. You will be taken back to medieval times and unlike other Moroccan Medina, the only means of transport are donkeys and mules to the extent that some of the biggest worldwide brands had to purchase their own mules to distribute the products inside.

Visit the tanneries where leather is being tanned using traditional methods while taking some amazing pictures from overlooking the terrace. Meander around the intricate alleyways and visit Museums, Souks, and Shrines.
In the late afternoon, we will escort you back to your accommodation.
Overnight accommodation in Riad El Yacout or similar- bed & breakfast option.

itinerary.label: Day 7
itinerary.title: FES - MIDDLE ATLAS - MIDELT - ZIZ VALLEY - MERZOUGA DESERT

description.text: After having breakfast in your Riad, you will head to the Sahara Desert crossing the lush Middle Atlas Mountains after having a pause for refreshment in Ifrane, the cleanest and Switzerland version town of Morocco.

The Middle Atlas is blessed with cedar forests that have been protected by UNESCO hosting a colony of Barbary Apes, which you can spot beside the road. After lunch in Midelt, you continue on the track further south through the Ziz Gorges and Palm Valley before reaching the dunes of Erg Chebbi that mark the end of today’s journey.
Upon arrival at Auberge de Sud (your hotel at the feet of the sand dunes), a warm welcome with mint tea while absorbing the exceptional beauty of the Sahara Desert.

The first thing that comes to every visitor’s mind is how outstandingly prevalent silence is forcing the soul to liberate itself from the burdens of life. Enjoy a nice dinner served by the pool followed by a percussion of drummers before spending some time contemplating the stars that illuminate the horizons.
Overnight accommodation in Riad Madu or similar – Half board option (dinner & breakfast are included).

itinerary.label: Day 8
itinerary.title: EXPLORE THE DESERT AREA & CAMEL TREK

description.text: After having breakfast in your Auberge, you will spend the day exploring the desert area and the palm oasis of Tafilalet starting with an interesting visit to the local aqueducts (Khettaras) – a sophisticated system of irrigation that consists of underground channels to convey water from afar to the oasis.

Continue on the track through the village of Merzouga to the Khamila Village where most of its residents have dark complexion because they were originally brought as slaves from Sub-Saharan land. They are known for the Gnawa Music that consists of drums and castanets, and which they happily perform to visitors.

If our day expedition coincides with the traditional weekly market that is used to taking place in Rissani, then you will have the chance to explore the Souk, which is organized into sections including dates, spices, vegetables, and much more.

In the afternoon, we drive back to the hotel to saddle up our camels for a journey to the camp that is located in the heart of the sand dunes of Erg Chebbi. Enjoy a nice dinner under the stars before ending the day with a nice sleep in the tent or under the stars.
Overnight accommodation in our luxury desert camp – Half Board option ( dinner & breakfast are included).
Early wake up in the morning to attend the majestic view of the sunrise over the dunes, then get back to the hotel by camel for a refreshing breakfast and to take a shower.

Drive to Dades Valley from Erfoud, Tinejdad, and Todra Gorges where you will stretch your legs through these impressive canyons that have attracted mountain climbers from all over the world as well as locals seeking cooler when it gets boiling in the summer.

After lunch, continue on the track to the Dades Valley where you will be assisted with luggage and formalities at the hotel. You may want to have a swim at the pool, relax, or stretch your legs down to the village of Boumalne Dades.
Overnight accommodation in Xaluca Dades or similar – Half Board option (dinner & breakfast are included)

itinerary.label: Day 10
itinerary.title: DADES VALLEY – VALLEY OF ROSES – SKOURA - OUARZAZATE

description.text: After having breakfast in your hotel/Riad, continue on the track further west through the road of one thousand Kasbahs. Form an idea behind the production of roses and the extracted products like rose water, soap, lotions, crèmes, and much more at the Valley of Roses. Visit the popular and well-preserved Kasbah of Amredil in Skoura before including a gentle hike at the Palmeraie where you will visit a local family and learn about the local history.

In the late afternoon, drive to Ouarzazate (Hollywood of Africa) where you will visit another Kasbah in the very heart of the city and was constructed by the Glaoui family who controlled the caravan route and with which they made a good fortune.
Overnight accommodation in Dar Chamaa or similar – Half board option (dinner & breakfast are included)

itinerary.label: Day 11
itinerary.title: OUARZAZATE - AIT BENHADDOU - ATLAS MOUNTAINS - MARRAKECH

description.text: After having breakfast in your Riad, head to Marrakech through the High Atlas Mountains after visiting the Atlas Film Studios (Optional) that have played a major role in filming a multitude of both national and international movies and documentaries.

Ait Benhaddou is the focal point of attraction for the day; as a result, you can’t miss exploring and wandering through the alleys of this dramatic village, which has been used by renowned producers in the field of cinema, as a special backdrop for shooting numerous Hollywood Movies including Gladiator, Lawrence of Arabia, The Kingdom of Heaven, Prince of Persia and many others.

After lunch, continue on the track following a less-traveled trail leading to the dramatic castle of Telouet, which powerfully depicts the glory and greatness of the Pasha El-Glaoui who could list himself as the wealthiest man in the world. Even though unfortunately, most of this structure is crumbling, a fact does not give you a margin to laughter but to contemplation and astonishment.

Visit the reception area and you will immediately be captivated by the geometric motifs, stucco, zellij tiles, and woodcarvings. Spacious rooms that are adorned differently reflect the power and wealth this man could get to the extent that he acquired the name of “The Lord of the Atlas and the South”.
Drive back to Marrakech through the spectacular Pass of Tizi n’Tichka and en route we will include stops for pictures and refreshments.
Overnight accommodation in Riad Ksar Anika or similar – bed & breakfast option.

Today, you will be having a full guided tour of this magical city of Marrakech starting with a nice drive through the wide boulevards of the Ville Nouvelle (New Town) that was initially built by the French when Morocco was under French rule from 1912 to 1956.

Visit the botanical gardens of Majorelle that took the painter Jacques Majorelle more than forty years of passion and dedication to come up with this unique masterpiece that outscores all of his paintings. Stretch your legs at the Menara Garden with its olive trees and orchards before embarking on a guided walking tour of the vibrant Medina of this unique city.

Begin at the Koutoubia Mosque, which is the landmark of Marrakech to the extent that it can be easily seen from different directions (by law, any building does not have to be higher than the minaret).

This Almohad masterpiece of architecture was built in the 12th century and used as a model for constructing numerous religious buildings worldwide. Visit the Saadian Tombs that are located at the Kasbah Quarter where your tour guide will share the history behind the Saadien Dynasty that ruled Morocco in the 15th and 16th centuries. The Bahia Palace is another attraction that reflects Moroccan and Moorish Architecture with its Riads, fountains, and gardens.

Wander around the intricate alleyways with its vibrant Souks that are organized into different sections including leather, spices, olives, clothing, vegetables, crafts, and much more. You will end your tour at the Square of Jemaa El Fna, which is the focal point of Marrakech that turns into a carnival of shows and exhibitions in which musicians, magicians, snake charmers, storytellers, fortunetellers, and acrobats give performances to the public along with the vibrant food stalls offering Moroccan delicacies.
TIP: Prior to sunset, you may want to enjoy the majestic view from atop Café De France, watching this cultural hub…
Overnight accommodation in Riad Ksar Anika or Similar – bed & breakfast accommodation.

After having breakfast in your Riad/Hotel, you may want to spend the first half day on your own maybe to further explore the Medina, do some shopping, go to a Hammam, or just relax at your accommodation.

At 1 pm, head west to the Essaouira “Wind City of Africa” which is at the Atlantic Coastline. An atmospheric fishing port with fortifications to protect its Medina from the strong waves being constructed according to the principles of contemporary European military architecture; however, it has retained a unique style and ambiance that inspired the hippies including Jimmy Hendrix who stayed here for some time.
The fortified Medina is easy to navigate and free of hassle compared to Marrakech, Fes, and Tangier. You may want to wander around its vibrant lanes, and sandy beach and visit the harbor.
Overnight accommodation in Hotel Riad Mimouna or similar – bed & breakfast option.

Spend the first half day chilling out in this magical town, and then drive further north along the Atlantic Coastline crossing Oualidia, which is known as the “Romantic Town” and El-Jadida was built by the Portuguese before getting to Casablanca.
Overnight accommodation in Kenzi Basma Hotel or similar – bed & breakfast option.
After having breakfast in your hotel, transfer to the airport in Casablanca and our Morocco trip will come to an end hoping you go back home with nice memories from Morocco.

faqs.question: What should I wear in Morocco, especially for women?

answer.text: Morocco is a conservative country, and it’s respectful to dress modestly, especially in more traditional areas. For women, this often means covering your shoulders, cleavage, and knees. It’s a good idea to carry a scarf or shawl for covering up when needed.

faqs.question: Is it safe to travel in Morocco?

answer.text: Morocco is generally safe for tourists. However, like any travel destination, it’s essential to take standard precautions such as safeguarding your belongings, avoiding isolated areas at night, and being aware of your surroundings.

faqs.question: What is the currency in Morocco, and where can I exchange money?

answer.text: The currency in Morocco is the Moroccan Dirham (MAD). You can exchange money at banks, exchange offices, and some hotels. ATMs are widely available, and credit cards are accepted in many places, especially in larger cities.

faqs.question: Is it necessary to know French or Arabic to travel in Morocco?

answer.text: While Arabic and Berber are the official languages, French is widely spoken, especially in cities and tourist areas. Many Moroccans in the tourism industry also speak English, making it relatively easy for English-speaking travelers to get by.

faqs.question: What is the etiquette for bargaining in Moroccan markets?

answer.text: Bargaining is a common practice in Moroccan markets (souks). Start by offering about half of the vendor’s initial price and be prepared to negotiate. It’s all part of the shopping experience, so don’t be afraid to haggle in a friendly manner.

segments.text: Why Would You Want to Book This Morocco Trip 15 Days/14 Nights?

You may be possibly thinking of taking a long flight to an exotic destination like Morocco and planning to make the most of your lifetime trip, then the Morocco Trip 15 days/14 nights is the one to vouch for. We have spent time and effort to carefully design this comprehensive tour based on firsthand experience aiming, therefore, to clear the ground for unique cultural immersions while enjoying the breathtaking views that Morocco has to offer.

This Morocco trip 15 days/14 nights covers three major geographical parts of this magical destination, you arrive at the heart of the economic capital of Morocco, then head further north while exploring Rabat, which is the UNESCO listed and the current administrative capital before continuing on the track to the charming city of Asilah. Tangier is also in the list and few people know how to taste the mystery of this city, get to the Andalusian and UNESCO Heritage World Site Medina of Tetouan before spending a full day meandering around the intricate streets of the blue-painted town of Chefchaouen.
Meet & Greet at the Airport of Casablanca
Visit the impressive Hassan II Mosque
Explore Oudayas Kasbah, Mohamed V Mausoleum, Hassan Tower in Rabat
Meander around the serene alleys of Asilah
Unveil the mystery of Tangier
Explore the intact Medina of Tetouan
Wander through the intricate streets of the blue-painted city of Chefchaouen
Camel trek & explore the desert area
Visit the canyons, Kasbah and Ksers
Have a guided tour around Marrakech “ Pearl of the South”

The alluring Meknes and Fes, former Imperial Capitals of Morocco cannot fail to haunt the souls of its visitors, be prepared to be taken back to Medieval Times. Cross the Middle Atlas Mountains, explore the Desert Area & Tafilalet Oasis before embarking on a lifetime journey in the Sahara Desert on a camel and spend the night under the stars in the heart of the desert. Visit the enchanting Kasbahs that are shrouded in mystery; however, our mission is to unveil to Moroccan history, culture, customs, traditions and much more.

Explore the Ait Benhaddou Kasbah that have been used as a backdrop for shooting numerous Hollywood Films including Lawrence of Arabia, Gladiator, Prince of Persia, and The Kingdom of Heaven and may others. The guided tour of Marrakech is another highlight that cannot be missed with its unique ambiance, culture and lifestyle.
DAY 1: ARRIVE IN CASABLANCA - RABAT

Upon arrival at the Mohamed V International Airport of Casablanca, your English-speaking private driver/guide – through his eyes, you will discover what Morocco has to offers – will meet and greet you before assisting you with luggage to the well-maintained SUV. Drive to the city center of Casablanca where you will have a tour of the impressive Hassan II Mosque before heading to Rabat where we will spend our first night.

Please note that it does actually depend on the time of your arrival since if it’s early during the day, then we may adjust the itinerary by providing additional services within Casablanca with no extra fees like visiting the Impressive Hassan II Mosque, drive through the Ain Diab Corniche and visit the popular Ricks Café. However, if it’s late we will then schedule such activities for the next day.
Overnight accommodation in a comfortable hotel/Riad including bed & breakfast.
DAY 2: CASABLANCA – RABAT – ASILAH - TANGIER

Begin your walking tour from the Oudayas Kasbah (small fortress) that was built initially by the Almoravid warriors to use as a base to organize attacks in Andalusia, then was rebuilt and expanded by the Almohads in the 12th century when the Sultan Yacoub El-Mansour (the Victorious) was planning to move the capital from Marrakech to Rabat.

Visit the impressive Hassan Tower, which forms a small portion of a great project of the largest mosque in the Islamic World; however, it did not come into existence because the Almohad Sultan passed away after three years of construction. Enjoy the breathtaking intricate motif designs within the white marble buildings of the late King Mohamed V Mausoleum.
Explore the best of Asilah

Continue on the track, after lunch, further north to the serene and tranquil Asilah with its whitewashed walls, which display an excellent range of paintings that have been skillfully stamped by international artists who are being invited annually to participate at the International Festival of Art. Enjoy the stunning views from the ramparts over the Atlantic Ocean before driving to Tangier, which is our final destination of the day.
Overnight accommodation in LaTangerina or similar – bed & breakfast option.
DAY3: TANGIER – TETOUAN - CHEFCHAOUEN- GUIDED TOUR OF CHEFCHAOUEN

After having breakfast in your Riad, spend the first half day exploring Tangier from the outside and inside covering the Cape Spartel where the Mediterranean and the Atlantic Ocean meet, and the pre-historic Hercules Caves before embarking on a nice Tangier guided walking tour (small fortress) that is panoramically perched uphill overlooking the vibrant Medina and Gibraltar.
Meander around the authentic Medina with its vibrant Souks (markets) that are organized into different sections before continuing on the track to the almost intact Medina of Tetouan.
EXPERIENCE THE BEST OF TETOUAN

Unlike most Medinas (old towns) of Morocco, the Medina of Tetouan remains smaller but has been almost untouched aside few buildings that were saved from dilapidation when it was listed by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site.

Tetouan was expanded by the expelled aristocratic families from Andalusia by the Spanish Reconquista, a fact that can be seen from the wide streets and big buildings that have marble fountains, carved ceilings, and groves planted with orange trees. Wander through its alleys, and vibrant small markets before continuing on the track to Chefchaouen via the Rif Mountains.
Overnight accommodation in Dar Echchaouen or similar – Half board option (dinner & breakfast are included)
DAY 4: FULL-DAY EXPLORING CHEFCHAOUEN

After having breakfast in your Riad, you will spend the day exploring this magical town that is nestled at the feet of two mountains with the shape of “goat’s horns” after which Chefchaouen was named because in Tamazight Language “Chaouen” means “Horns”.

You will be captivated by the prevalent blue color with which it is painted; meander through the beautifully painted streets with its shutters and wrought iron windows to the natural spring of Ras El-Ma where you can spot women washing clothes and carpets, and most of the time boys play soccer nearby.
Your private tour guide will give you an insight into the history behind the foundation of Chefchaouen as a Kasbah (small fortress) to fight against the Portuguese invasion.

You will visit this Kasbah which is located at the very heart of the Old Medina before ending your guided walking tour at the famous Utta El-Hammam Square. You may want to have lunch at one of the small restaurants overlooking the Kasbah and Mosque while watching the passers-by.

In the late afternoon, the Medina of Chefchaouen gets vibrant with its small shops selling all kinds of stuff from fruits, vegetables, crafts, electronics, clothes, and much more. You may want to have another taste of this unique lifestyle on your own before you get back to your Riad.
Overnight accommodation in Dar Echchaouen or similar – bed & breakfast option.
DAY 5: CHEFCHAOUEN – VOLUBILIS – MEKNES - FES

After having breakfast in your Riad, you will be picked up by your private driver to continue on the track further south by crossing the spectacular Rif Mountains from where you get to the popular Roman Ruins of Volubilis. This archaeological site is located in the very heart of fertile land planted with olive trees and orchards at the feet of the Zerhoun Mountain. It reveals a rich history of the Romans that occupied the north of Morocco and therefore powerfully influenced the lifestyle of the Amazigh people.

The archaeological local tour guide will unveil the mystery of this site before continuing to Meknes, which is one of the most important cities in Morocco It is one of the four imperial capitals that witnessed its glory and golden age during the reign of the Alaouite Sultan Moulay Ismail in the 17th century.

Begin your tour of Meknes from the beautiful gate of Bab Al-Mansour (Victorious) that overlooks the Hedim Square, which Sultan Moulay Ismail used for army parades and exposition. Visit the Sultan’s Mausoleum with its exquisite geometric designs depicting a mix of Moroccan and Andalusian architectures. Drive through the walls of the Royal Palace to the popular granaries that are used for storing grains, and stables for looking after the famous 12,000 royal horses before taking the highway to Fes, which is our final destination today.
Overnight accommodation in Riad El Yacout or similar – bed & breakfast option.
DAY 6: FULL-DAY EXPLORING FES

After having breakfast in your Riad, you will have a fully guided & purely cultural day tour of Fes with a professional local tour guide whose knowledge about the history and lifestyle of the city is outstanding. Drive uphill to catch the panoramic view of Fes El-Bali (Old Medina), which is one of the most car-free urban centers in the world.

Stretch your legs by the Mellah (former Jewish Quarter) where you will get an insight into the Jewish Community that settled in Fes before moving to Israel in 1948. It’s possible to visit the synagogue and take nice shots by the bronze gates of the Royal Palace.

Embark on a guided walking tour of this magical Medina that has gained popularity worldwide due to the exotic experience it offers. You will be taken back to medieval times and unlike other Moroccan Medina, the only means of transport are donkeys and mules to the extent that some of the biggest worldwide brands had to purchase their own mules to distribute the products inside.

Visit the tanneries where leather is being tanned using traditional methods while taking some amazing pictures from overlooking the terrace. Meander around the intricate alleyways and visit Museums, Souks, and Shrines.
In the late afternoon, we will escort you back to your accommodation.
Overnight accommodation in Riad El Yacout or similar- bed & breakfast option.
DAY 7: FES - MIDDLE ATLAS - MIDELT - ZIZ VALLEY - MERZOUGA DESERT

After having breakfast in your Riad, you will head to the Sahara Desert crossing the lush Middle Atlas Mountains after having a pause for refreshment in Ifrane, the cleanest and Switzerland version town of Morocco.

The Middle Atlas is blessed with cedar forests that have been protected by UNESCO hosting a colony of Barbary Apes, which you can spot beside the road. After lunch in Midelt, you continue on the track further south through the Ziz Gorges and Palm Valley before reaching the dunes of Erg Chebbi that mark the end of today’s journey.
Upon arrival at Auberge de Sud (your hotel at the feet of the sand dunes), a warm welcome with mint tea while absorbing the exceptional beauty of the Sahara Desert.

The first thing that comes to every visitor’s mind is how outstandingly prevalent silence is forcing the soul to liberate itself from the burdens of life. Enjoy a nice dinner served by the pool followed by a percussion of drummers before spending some time contemplating the stars that illuminate the horizons.
Overnight accommodation in Riad Madu or similar – Half board option (dinner & breakfast are included).
DAY 8: EXPLORE THE DESERT AREA & CAMEL TREK

After having breakfast in your Auberge, you will spend the day exploring the desert area and the palm oasis of Tafilalet starting with an interesting visit to the local aqueducts (Khettaras) – a sophisticated system of irrigation that consists of underground channels to convey water from afar to the oasis.

Continue on the track through the village of Merzouga to the Khamila Village where most of its residents have dark complexion because they were originally brought as slaves from Sub-Saharan land. They are known for the Gnawa Music that consists of drums and castanets, and which they happily perform to visitors.

If our day expedition coincides with the traditional weekly market that is used to taking place in Rissani, then you will have the chance to explore the Souk, which is organized into sections including dates, spices, vegetables, and much more.

In the afternoon, we drive back to the hotel to saddle up our camels for a journey to the camp that is located in the heart of the sand dunes of Erg Chebbi. Enjoy a nice dinner under the stars before ending the day with a nice sleep in the tent or under the stars.
Overnight accommodation in our luxury desert camp – Half Board option ( dinner & breakfast are included).
DAY 9: MERZOUGA – TODRA GORGES – DADES VALLEY
Early wake up in the morning to attend the majestic view of the sunrise over the dunes, then get back to the hotel by camel for a refreshing breakfast and to take a shower.

Drive to Dades Valley from Erfoud, Tinejdad, and Todra Gorges where you will stretch your legs through these impressive canyons that have attracted mountain climbers from all over the world as well as locals seeking cooler when it gets boiling in the summer.

After lunch, continue on the track to the Dades Valley where you will be assisted with luggage and formalities at the hotel. You may want to have a swim at the pool, relax, or stretch your legs down to the village of Boumalne Dades.
Overnight accommodation in Xaluca Dades or similar – Half Board option (dinner & breakfast are included)
DAY 10: DADES VALLEY – VALLEY OF ROSES – SKOURA - OUARZAZATE

After having breakfast in your hotel/Riad, continue on the track further west through the road of one thousand Kasbahs. Form an idea behind the production of roses and the extracted products like rose water, soap, lotions, crèmes, and much more at the Valley of Roses. Visit the popular and well-preserved Kasbah of Amredil in Skoura before including a gentle hike at the Palmeraie where you will visit a local family and learn about the local history.

In the late afternoon, drive to Ouarzazate (Hollywood of Africa) where you will visit another Kasbah in the very heart of the city and was constructed by the Glaoui family who controlled the caravan route and with which they made a good fortune.

overview.text: Private Benalmadena to Morocco Day Trip

Experience the magic of Morocco on a private Benalmadena to Morocco day trip designed for comfort and adventure. We’ll pick you up directly from your chosen address in Benalmadena and drive along the scenic coastline to the port of Tarifa. There, you’ll board the 9 a.m. fast ferry for a short and exciting ride across the Strait of Gibraltar to Tangier.

Once in Morocco, your local guide will welcome you and lead you on a journey through the vibrant streets of Tangier. Explore the historic Kasbah, wander through the colorful Medina, and visit iconic sites like Cap Spartel and the Hercules Caves. Enjoy a traditional Moroccan lunch, take in the rich culture, and even hop on a short camel ride before heading back. This private day trip offers a seamless, personalized experience from Spain to Africa—all in one unforgettable day.

description.text: Please expect your private driver to pick you up from your chosen address in Benalmadena before heading to the Tarifa Port for a memorable Benalmadena to Morocco day trip. The drive is around 2 hours, and once you arrive in the Tarifa port, you will board the 09 a.m. ferry.

Your boarding passes will be shared with you by email and on WhatsApp. After embarking on the ferry at 09 a.m., please get your passports stamped, then enjoy the crossing across the Strait of Gibraltar to the continent of Africa.

description.text: Once you step foot in Morocco, your private tour guide will meet and greet you holding a welcoming sign displaying your name. Your all-inclusive Benalmadena to Morocco day trip includes a scenic drive through the New Town (Ville Nouvelle), palaces, and Perdicars Park before reaching the promontory Cape of Spartel, where it is believed the Mediterranean and the Atlantic seas converge. After enjoying the breathtaking views while having a refreshing breakfast, you will go on a camel ride experience on the sandy beach of the Atlantic, then continue on the track to make a short visit to the Neolithic Hercules Caves.

Your Tangier day trip from Benalmadena will include a guided tour of the dramatic Kasbah with its narrow alleyways, which are shrouded in mystery. Visit the Kasbah Museum , which is a Palace inhabited by the late Sultan Moulay Ismail in the 17th century, and exhibits a wide range of ancient Moroccan antiques reflecting the rich culture.
After lunch in a nice Moroccan restaurant, your private tour of Tangier will take you to the vibrant Medina with its colorful Souks, alleyways

The private Benalmadena to Morocco day trip will come to its end when your tour guide escorts you to the port to board the 4 p.m. Arrive in Tarifa at around 6 p.m., meet your driver and head back to Benalmadena, hoping you have an enjoyable day trip in the charming Tangier.

body.text: "Our trip with Tangier Excursions was incredible - from initial planning, execution, and communication, the whole process was extremely seamless and professional. Even when we had a change of plans and had to adjust timing, they were very accommodating and updated our itinerary to make the most of our experience. The guides in both Chefchaouen (Abdenour) and Tangier (Mohamed) were amazing, and made us feel like we were seeing all the best parts of the city. Couldn’t have asked for a better experience, and can’t wait to go back!"
ALLY BEST USA
