Please note that your private tour guide will be waiting for you at the Tangier Ville port’s terminal holding a signboard with your name on it. In case you can’t find your guide, you might get approached by other fellow tour guides. As a result, please try to avoid them and immediately reach out to us at +212 666-941294, and we will effectively remedy any issue.
1. Passport & Visa Requirements

A valid passport is required for all travelers. Please ensure your passport is valid for at least 6 months beyond your travel date. Some nationalities may also need a visa to enter Morocco — please check with your local embassy or consulate in advance.
2. Early Departure Time

This tour starts early with a pick-up at 6:45 A.M. from your accommodation in the Cadiz area. Be sure to get enough rest the night before and be ready on time to ensure a smooth journey to the ferry port in Tarifa.
3. Ferry Duration
The ferry from Tarifa to Tangier takes approximately 1 hour . It’s a comfortable ride, but if you are prone to motion sickness, we recommend bringing appropriate medication just in case.
4. Clothing & Comfort

We recommend wearing comfortable walking shoes and weather-appropriate clothing . Morocco is generally warm, but coastal winds can make it feel cooler, especially in the mornings. A light jacket is useful, even in summer.
5. Currency & Payments

The local currency in Morocco is the Moroccan Dirham (MAD) . You don’t need to exchange a lot — most tourist shops accept euros , but having some small change in local currency is helpful for tips or small purchases. Your guide can assist you if needed.
6. Language
Your Tangier guide speaks English, Spanish, and French , so communication is easy. In the Medina, people often speak Arabic or Berber, but your guide will help translate.
7. Food & Dining

Lunch is not included unless arranged in advance. Your guide will recommend a safe, authentic Moroccan restaurant where you can enjoy a traditional meal like tagine or couscous. Let us know in advance if you have any dietary restrictions (vegetarian, gluten-free, etc.).
8. Walking & Activity Level

The walking tour includes some cobblestone streets and slight hills , especially in the Kasbah. Guests should be able to walk at a moderate pace. If you have mobility concerns , please let us know so we can adapt the tour.
9. Camel Ride
The camel ride by the beach is short and optional but fun for all ages! Great for photos and a memorable part of the experience. If you prefer not to ride, you can enjoy the scenery instead.
10. Return & Timing

Your guide will ensure you return to the Tangier port on time for the 3:00 P.M. ferry . After arriving in Tarifa, your private driver will take you directly back to Cadiz, arriving in the evening around 7:00–8:00 P.M.

itinerary.title: MEET & GREET AT THE PORT OF TANGIER

description.text: This private day trip to Morocco from Spain offers the first opportunity to step foot on the African continent. Upon arrival at the port of Tangier, you will be met & greeted by your private English-speaking tour guide who is going to unveil the mystery of Tangier and Morocco in general.

Drive through the Ville Nouvelle “New Town” to get a close glimpse of modern life, then through the California district, Royal Palace before getting to Cape Spartel promontory. The view of the sea, from this point, is mesmerizing, stretching as far as the eye can see.

The lighthouse reveals interesting history as it was first illuminated in 1864 after four years of hard work and negotiations among representatives of nine European powers, the USA & Morocco. You will be served soft drinks & pastries before continuing on the track along the Atlantic shoreline to experience a camel ride by the sandy beach.

Drive further to Hercules Caves that go back to the Neolithic Era, with two openings, one to land and one to sea, known as “The Map of Africa”. The beauty of the caves can easily catch your eye but you will do more when the tour guide unfolds its mysteries.

itinerary.title: EXPLORE THE KASBAH & THE MEDINA OF TANGIER

description.text: Drive back to the Kasbah where you will have a nice strolling tour through the narrow streets, where you will find the Kasbah Museum. This immensely beautiful former Royal Palace goes back to the 17th century when Sultan Moulay Ismail used it as a home. The incredible architecture and the traditional courtyard along with the fountain are just stunning.

Strolling through the narrow alleyways of the Ancient Medina is a kind of a must-do as it makes you travel back in time to its heyday in the 17th century. Your tour guide will introduce you to the first communal bakery or oven that is still working to this day baking bread for the locals.

Continue on the track through the vibrant and colorful Souks selling everything from spices, herbs, vegetables, fish, slippers, rugs, meat, and much more. From the Petit Socco , you will get to the Grand Socco , a big square that was formerly the biggest market in Tangier. An ideal spot for locals to go to relax and sit down while watching the passers-by (we highly recommend doing so).

Make a visit to the American Legation , which turned into a museum, and is the first official American property built outside of the United States. Morocco was the first country to recognize the Independence of the United States; this building is an eyewitness to the historic cultural & diplomatic relations between the two countries.

Drive from Medina to the New Town where you will have a nice lunch served in a Moroccan restaurant. Now, you will cherish the traditional Moroccan cuisine. Culminate the meal with a delicious min tea before driving back to the port where we will assist you with the customs.

reviews.title: Be prepared to be amazed...
reviews.text:
After our private day trip in Tangier with Abu, we agreed that everyone visiting should know what a great experience he provided.

Meeting us at the ferry, Abu drove us to places we would have never found on our own and shared his knowledge of history, culture, education, and lifestyles. From the heart of the city through beautiful parks and communities and out to the ocean we discovered Tangier.

Then we parked and wandered past homes, ancient walls, mosques, museums and shops along the stone paths and narrow roads in the Kasbah and Central Markets. Abu consulted with us on what we wanted to include in the day (I really did want to ride a camel on the beach, to drink mint tea and have a henna design on my hand – and we so we did). We could not have been happier.

It was a day we will never forget!

We had a great day trip exploring Tangier. Our guide, Abu, met us at the port and he and a driver took us all around the city, This is the absolute best way to see the highlights of Tangier in only one day. Abu was very informative and his English was great. We enjoyed all the stops along the way, especially the camel ride on the beach and the delicious Moroccan lunch overlooking the Mediterranean. We stopped by the Caves of Hercules and the view was breathtaking. The walking tour through the city was a great experience, hearing the call for prayer that is done five times each day, seeing the snake charmer, visiting the markets and seeing the people of Tangier in their colorful clothing going about their daily business. The day trip to Tangier with Abu as our guide was definitely worth every penny and one of the highlights of our vacation. I would highly recommend this to anyone.

I and my family had a great luxury tour of Tangier that was arranged for us by Tangier Excursions. Our guide, Abu, was informative, friendly and courteous. We can’t recommend this company enough (:

itinerary.title: Meet and greet at the port of Tangier

description.text: Depart from Tarifa to Tangier across the strait of Gibraltar where you will meet your English-speaking private tour guide with whom you will spend the day out exploring the majestic Tangier and Asilah. Begin your journey with the sightseeing tour around Tangier by driving through the Ville Nouvelle (New Town) that was built by the European International Powers. You will learn how the political system did work during that time in which the peaceful co-existence prevailed.

Drive through the French, Italian, Dutch, Belgium, Spanish & British former and uphill through the fertile and lush forest where numerous fancy palaces and mansions including the Royal Palace are built.

Have some time for refreshment at the Cape Spartel where it is believed at this point both the Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea converge. It is possible to experience the camel ride by the sandy beach or take pictures before continuing on the track to the Hercules Caves that date back to the Neolithic Era.

itinerary.title: Guided Walking Tour of the Kasbah & Medina

description.text: Drive back to the Kasbah for an interesting stroll around its intricate alleys where you will notice that most of the buildings have been transformed into boutique hotels, Riad, restaurants, or private residences. Visit the Kasbah Museum which served as a Royal Residence (Dar El Makhzan) during the era of Moulay Ismail in the 17th century. The Kasbah Museums displays an excellent collection of antiques and relics witnessing the rich history of the north, you will also learn about the architecture and traditional layouts of Moroccan Palaces. The view of the Medina (Old Town), Gibraltar and Spain are stunning from here.

Wander the Medina with its narrow alleyways and the buildings forming a mixture of Moroccan, Andalusian & European styles of architecture. It forms the most traditional commercial hub of Tangier being centered by the Petit Socco and is divided into five main quarters; the Souks (markets) are also divided into sections such as fish, vegetable, antique, spice markets, and many others.

itinerary.title: Explore the artistic city of Asilah

description.text: After lunch, resume your journey along the Atlantic Coastline to Asilah, which is one of the most charming, transfixing and romantic cities in the north of Morocco. It’s a haven for tranquility, serenity and inner peace. Stroll through its tranquil streets and painted walls. Asilah is popular for the International Cultural Festival of Asilah, Morocco that is being held every year honoring the traditional lifestyle of the town dwellers and the art of painting to the extent that it has been turned into an open museum of art depicting different aspects of our lives.

The popular Tangier and Tetouan day trip from Gibraltar, Sevilla, Malaga, Tarifa…etc is carefully designed to allow you to meet the real Moroccan hospitality on its own terms opening wide gates of discovery and opening up.
Tangier & Tetouan are the largest cities in the north of Morocco but still shrouded in mystery as most visitors mistakenly dismiss the available opportunity to experience an intact culture.

itinerary.title: Meet and greet at the port of Tangier

description.text: The Tangier and Tetouan day trip from Gibraltar, Marbella, Malaga, Seville, Tarifa…etc remains one of the most popular day trips to Morocco from Spain and is carefully designed to enable you to experience what the mysterious cities of Tangier and Tetouan have to offer.

links.text: day trips to Morocco from Spain

description.text: The most recommended way to get to Tangier from Spain is by fast ferry from Tarifa Port as the journey takes around 45 minutes. Upon arrival at the dock of Tangier, you will notice your private tour guide holding a sign with your name on it.

You will initially explore the Ville Nouvelle “New Town”, which was primarily built by International Powers that ruled the city from 1920th to 1950th and this fact is noticeable to this day with districts being named after countries that had offices in the area such French, Belgium, Spanish, Dutch…Districts. Drive through the area where richest Moroccans & foreigners live with its fancy villas, mansions & palaces.

Your guided tour of Tangier will take you to the Cap Spartel where it is believed at this exact point both the Atlantic & Mediterranean Seas converge. The lighthouse that still serves the ships & boats crossing the Strait of Gibraltar functions in a traditional way since 1864. Enjoy a nice mint tea along with the stunning views. After that, you may want to experience the camel ride by the sandy beach before making a visit to the pre-historic Hercules Caves.

itinerary.title: Guided Walking Tour of the Kasbah & Medina

description.text: The second part of our guided tour of Tangier will take us to the dramatic Kasbah (small fortress) that is perched uphill overlooking the Medina, Gibraltar, Spain & the Atlantic Ocean.

Meander around the small lanes with its white buildings that have been turned into Hotel Riads or private residences. Visit the Kasbah Museum that served as a royal residence during the reign of Moulay Ismail in the 17th century and the current museums beautifully display a wide selection of antiques, crafts, jewelry, pottery that reveal the ancient and rich history of the northern part of Morocco.

Continue your walk, following the instructions of your private tour guide, down using hundreds of steps to the vibrant Medina that has been the hub for cultural & commercial activities. The Souks (markets) are organized into sections based on the products on sales such as vegetables, fish, spices, crafts, clothes and much more.

itinerary.title: Explore the UNESCO Listed Heritage World Medina of Tetouan

description.text: Our day trip to Tangier & Tetouan from Gibraltar will take us now to Tetouan through the speedy road. You will spend your time exploring this magical city that has been called “ Little Jerusalem ” or “ Daughter of Granada ”.

The Medina (Old Town) is somehow the smallest compared to other Moroccan old towns but has been almost untouched since its foundation apart from few buildings that were saved by the UNESCO . Tetouan was expanded by the Jewish & Moorish Aristocrats who were expelled from Andalusia during the Reconquista, a fact that can be seen from the interior of some of its buildings with its wrought iron grills, stucco work, woodcarvings, Zelij tiles and much more.

Wander around the narrow lanes of the ancient and learn about the history behind the foundation of the Medina. Visit the Souks before we drive back to Tangier where we will assist you at the port for your departure.

By the end of the day, the Tangier and Tetouan day trip should have brought the rich history, culture & lifestyle of the northern part of Morocco alive to you. Please note we do also offer short trips from Tangier in case you have more time to explore Asilah, Chefchaouen or even the Imperial Cities of Morocco.

faqs.question: How far is Morocco from Spain?

answer.text: Morocco is the closest point to the African continent from Spain and Europe. The distance between Tangier (in the north of Morocco) and Tarifa (in the south of Spain) is around 15 kms (9.32 miles).

faqs.question: How long is the ferry ride from Tarifa to Tangier?

answer.text: Normally, it takes around an hour including the customs.

faqs.question: How do I get from Spain to Tangier and Tetouan?

answer.text: Most day trips depart via ferry from Tarifa or Algeciras (Spain) to Tangier (Morocco) (Tarifa is recommended) . The ferry ride takes approximately 1 hour from Tarifa or 1.5–2 hours from Algeciras . Transfers between cities (Tangier to Tetouan) are typically included in guided tours, with a 1-hour drive between them.

faqs.question: Do you offer shared tours?

answer.text: Since the foundation of Tangier Excursions LLC back in 2015, our commitment to offering, quality services while allowing our dear customers experience Tangier and Morocco intimately, has been always the same. We provide private and shared tour of Tangier without sacrificing the delivery of quality services..

faqs.question: Do I need a passport or visa for this trip?

answer.text: Yes, a valid passport is required. Most nationalities (e.g., EU, US, Canada) receive a 90-day visa-free entry to Morocco. Ensure your passport is stamped upon arrival. Check visa requirements for your nationality in advance.

faqs.question: What are the top sights in Tangier and Tetouan?

answer.text: Tangier: The historic Medina, Kasbah Museum, Hercules Caves, and Cap Spartel.
Tetouan: UNESCO-listed Medina, Royal Palace (exterior), and artisan markets for ceramics and textiles.

faqs.question: Can I use euros in Morocco?

answer.text: The local currency is the Moroccan Dirham (MAD) . Some shops accept euros, but exchange dirhams for better rates. ATMs and exchange bureaus are available in Tangier.

Lunch at a local spot (the lamb tagine!) was divine, and Tetouan’s quieter, artsy Medina felt like stepping into a hidden world. Bought stunning ceramics and laughed my way through bargaining—thanks to Amina’s tips! Long day, but worth every second. Pro tip: Pack comfy shoes and an empty bag for souvenirs. Can’t recommend enough!

Absolutely! The trip is private and flexible, making it ideal for families, couples, or small groups of friends. Children usually love the camel ride and exploring the medina.
What currency should I bring to Morocco?
The local currency is the Moroccan Dirham (MAD). Some shops may accept euros, but it’s best to have some local cash if you plan to shop in the souks.
Can I book this tour last minute?
We recommend booking at least 48 hours in advance to ensure availability and allow time for ferry ticket arrangements.

reviews.title: Great Tour!
reviews.text: Mohammed gave us a great tour around Tangier. He was knowledgeable and customized the tour to our interests. His English was excellent as well. The driver was very safe and courteous. He realized we were Jewish and made sure that we got to see the beautiful synagogues in the area. That was very special. We particularly enjoyed seeing the kindness to animals and tolerance of all religious there. My only complaint is that we didn’t have any menu items to choose from for lunch. As we did request, spicy Moroccan food on our form, needless to say, the CousCous was delicious. Would highly recommend!
reviews.name: Laurel W

reviews.title: Great Personal Service
reviews.text: We were met by Mohamed as we got off the ferry from Tarifa and escorted to a van with a driver. This was great because it enabled Mohamed to focus his attention on introducing us to Tangier. Mohamed pointed out some of the luxury celebrity housing on our way to our camel ride. It’;s a very touristy thing to do but I’m very glad I did it. It’s very different from riding a horse and the experience of the camel getting to its feet and then later getting back down is special. We were taken to breakfast where we had mint tea and camel cheese on some very good bread. Camel cheese is quite mild and very good. Mohamed gave us a thorough tour in the time we had. When it was time to go he escorted us through customs to the front of the ferry line. We were the first ones on for the return trip. April 2023
reviews.name: Jack Cannata

reviews.title: Absolutely fantastic!
reviews.text: We contacted Tangier Excursions after deciding we’d like to try an overnight stay in Morocco whilst on holiday in Spain. Moha responded immediately giving us loads of confidence, recommending what we should do and then very swiftly organised absolutely everything for us. We were met by a driver in a very smart Mercedes van at Tangier port, tour guides showed us around and we had a wonderful overnight stay in the blue city of Chechaouen. An amazing experience and so straight forward thanks to Moha! I’d highly recommend Tangier Excursions.
reviews.name: CJ Neale

reviews.title: Wonderful Experience
reviews.text: Tangier Excursions is the consummate professional tour operator. Moha was very prompt, responding to all emails and taking care of the ferry tickets from Tarifa, and had a car waiting when we arrived, making everything simple. For the day-long tour, our guide was Mohamed and the gentleman was very friendly and extremely knowledgeable about the history of the country. We did a car tour in the morning (very nice) and a walking tour around the city in the afternoon. There were various stops for food and drinks, all of which were quite good. For first-time visitors to Morocco like ourselves, it opened our eyes to the beauty of the area. Thank you Moha! We will be back in Morocco some time again!.

description.text: Today, your private driver will pick you up from your accommodation in Malaga at 05:30 am before embarking on your interesting Malaga to Morocco day trip. The journey takes around 2 hours to get to the Tarifa port to get your ferry to Tangier Ville Port.

Once you cross the Strait of Gibraltar and your ferry docks in the Tangier Ville Port, you will meet up with your private and local tour guide (The guide will be holding a signboard with your name on it).

Have a drive through the Ville Nouvelle (New Town) of Tangier which was built by the eight powers that ruled. The architecture as well as the signs still witness an era of opening up and peaceful coexistence among myriad cultures in a small geographical location.

Our private Malaga day to Morocco will take us to the promontory Cap Spartel where you can enjoy stunning views of the Atlantic and the Mediterranean. Enjoy nice Moroccan snacks and drinks before going on a camel ride experience by the sandy beach of the Atlantic.
Later, we will visit the Neolithic Hercules Caves which are shrouded in mystery before continuing on the track back to the mysterious Kasbah and Medina of Tangier.

itinerary.title: EXPLORE THE KASBAH & THE MEDINA OF TANGIER

description.text: Drive back to the Kasbah where you will have a nice strolling tour through the narrow streets, where you will find the Kasbah Museum. This immensely beautiful former Royal Palace goes back to the 17th century when Sultan Moulay Ismail used it as a home. The incredible architecture and the traditional courtyard along with the fountain are just stunning.

Strolling through the narrow alleyways of the Ancient Medina is a kind of a must-do as it makes you travel back in time to its heyday in the 17th century. Your tour guide will introduce you to the first communal bakery or oven that is still working to this day baking bread for the locals.

Continue on the track through the vibrant and colorful Souks selling everything from spices, herbs, vegetables, fish, slippers, rugs, meat, and much more. From the Petit Socco , you will get to the Grand Socco , a big square that was formerly the biggest market in Tangier. An ideal spot for locals to go to relax and sit down while watching the passers-by (we highly recommend doing so).

Visit the American Legation , which turned into a museum, and is the first official American property built outside of the United States. Morocco was the first country to recognize the Independence of the United States; this building is an eyewitness to the historic cultural & diplomatic relations between the two countries.

Drive from Medina to the New Town where you will have a nice lunch served in a Moroccan restaurant. Now, you will cherish traditional Moroccan cuisine. Culminate the meal with a delicious min tea before driving back to the port where we will assist you with the customs.

Please note in case you are devoting more than one day to Morocco in your travel schedule, we have also put together well-crafted itineraries from Short Trips from Tangier to Private Morocco Tours from anywhere in Morocco.

overview.text: Private Rota to Morocco Day Trip

If you’re looking to add an unforgettable cultural twist to your holiday in southern Spain, our private Rota to Morocco day trip is your perfect escape. This immersive experience takes you from the calm shores of Rota to the exotic rhythms of Tangier in just one day. Cross the Strait of Gibraltar in comfort and step into the charm of Moroccan heritage—guided by locals who know every secret alley, story, and scent of this North African gem.

Unlike standard tours, this day trip from Rota to Morocco is designed for curious travelers who crave authentic moments. From camel rides on the beach to the colorful souks of Tangier, you’ll explore vibrant traditions, ancient sites, and delicious cuisine. Whether you’re traveling as a couple, family, or small group, this Rota to Tangier day trip offers a private, flexible, and enriching experience you’ll always remember.

description.text: Your day begins early with a comfortable pick-up from your selected address in Rota. Sit back and enjoy the scenic drive through the Andalusian countryside on your way to the Tarifa port.
Your ferry tickets will be provided in advance via email. You’ll board the 9:00 A.M. fast ferry to Tangier, a journey of around one hour across the Strait of Gibraltar.

itinerary.title: ARRIVE IN TANGIER & TOUR THE CITY

description.text: At the Tangier Ville Port, your private Moroccan guide will greet you with a welcome sign. Start your Rota to Tangier day trip by exploring the scenic coast and city landmarks. You’ll drive past historic palaces, stop at Perdicaris Park for nature views, and continue to the majestic Cape Spartel, where the Atlantic Ocean meets the Mediterranean Sea. Then, enjoy a traditional camel ride along the beach before heading to the famous Hercules Caves , rich in legend and natural beauty.

Next, step into Tangier’s Old Town for a guided walk through the Kasbah and Medina . Discover hidden gems in the maze-like streets, visit the vibrant souks, and admire the colorful architecture. Learn about local life and stop for a traditional Moroccan lunch (optional, not included).

After a full day of discovery, your guide will accompany you back to the Tangier port. You’ll board the return ferry to Tarifa, where your private driver will be waiting. From there, you’ll be taken back to Rota and dropped off at your chosen address, ending your day trip from Rota to Morocco in comfort and style.

segments.text: Private Rota to Morocco Day Trip

If you’re looking to add an unforgettable cultural twist to your holiday in southern Spain, our private Rota to Morocco day trip is your perfect escape. This immersive experience takes you from the calm shores of Rota to the exotic rhythms of Tangier in just one day. Cross the Strait of Gibraltar in comfort and step into the charm of Moroccan heritage—guided by locals who know every secret alley, story, and scent of this North African gem.

Unlike standard tours, this day trip from Rota to Morocco is designed for curious travelers who crave authentic moments. From camel rides on the beach to the colorful souks of Tangier, you’ll explore vibrant traditions, ancient sites, and delicious cuisine. Whether you’re traveling as a couple, family, or small group, this Rota to Tangier day trip offers a private, flexible, and enriching experience you’ll always remember.

The guides in both Chefchaouen (Abdenour) and Tangier (Mohamed) were amazing, and made us feel like we were seeing all the best parts of the city. Couldn’t have asked for a better experience, and can’t wait to go back!"

body.text: Diana Fung Hong Kong
Pick-up from Seville at 05:30 A.M.

Your private driver will pick you up from the address of your choice in Seville before embarking on this Tangier day trip from Seville, and let the magic of Morocco add an extraordinary chapter to your travel tale. It’s more than just a trip; it’s a rendezvous with two worlds, harmonizing for a fleeting yet unforgettable encounter.
Heading to Tarifa Port: A Gateway to Adventure

The road to Tarifa port unfolds before you, offering scenic vistas that mirror the excitement within. At 9 AM, you step onto the ferry, and as it sets sail across the Strait of Gibraltar, you’re transported not only geographically but also culturally. The waves of the Mediterranean and Atlantic dance around you, as if echoing the harmonization of Spain and Morocco on this remarkable day.
Arrive in Tarifa Port

Upon arrival in Tangier, your journey takes an enchanting turn as you’re welcomed by a local private tour guide who will meet and greet you holding a welcoming sign with your name on it. With infectious enthusiasm, they become your bridge to Tangier’s heart and soul. Their stories paint vivid images of the city’s history and modern life, and you realize that this day is not just a tour but a chance to connect.
Exploring Cap Spartel: Where Land Meets Sky

The first stop is Cap Spartel, where the Atlantic Ocean and Mediterranean Sea embrace in an awe-inspiring display of nature’s grandeur. You stand at the edge of two worlds, a powerful metaphor for the day’s theme. The panoramic view of the vast blue expanse invigorates your spirit, preparing you for the wonders that lie ahead.
Camel Ride by the Atlantic: A Taste of the Exotic

Embrace an exhilarating camel ride by the sandy shores of the Atlantic—a genuine Moroccan experience that you’ll cherish. The rhythmic sway of the camel echoes the beating of your heart, and as you traverse the shoreline, the wind carries whispers of ancient tales. description.text: Experience the Real Tangier with our Tangier Guided Tour

Depart from Tarifa to Tangier by the fast ferry (it takes normally around one hour) and upon arrival; you will meet with your private tour guide whom you will notice holding a sign with your name on it. Otherwise, you will be collected from your accommodation in Tangier by prior arrangement.

The first part of this interesting Guided walking tour of Tangier will take you to the Kasbah that is perched uphill and was historically used as a defense station. It overlooks panoramically the Medina (Old Town), Gibraltar, and Spain, and the view from this point is stunning.

You will notice that most of the Kasbah have been converted into private homes for foreigners and boutique hotels; however, this fact does not prevent any visitor to learn about the rich history behind its foundation, particularly if you are accompanied by a local tour guide who grew up within the walls of this area.

Follow your guide through the intricate alleyways to the Palace Du Mechouar, which is a square in the very heart of the Kasbah that served as a parade ground whenever the late Alaouite Sultan Moulay Ismail used to visit Tangier in the 17th century.

Visit the Kasbah Museum that was originally the residence for the Sultan Moulay Ismail and has been recently converted into an interesting museum housing various relics that go back to the Stone Age through the turn of the 20th century. It reveals powerfully the rich history of Tangier and the North of Morocco in general through a wide collection of antiques, manuscripts, crafts, and much more. It opens from Wednesday through Monday from 09:00 am to 4 PM and the Admission fee is 20 MAD.

Wander around the Medina (Old Town) that is divided into five main quarters and centered by the vibrant Petit Socco Square where you may be invited by your tour guide to sit in a café, order a sweet min tea, and watch people. You will then explore the Souks (Markets) that are divided into sections according to specialties such as fish, vegetables, spices, crafts, and much more.
After your guided walking tour of Tangier Medina , your private tour guide will make sure to escort you back to the port, accommodation, or farewell you at the location of your choice.

You may want to opt for the full-day trip to Tangier from Tarifa, Spain , or an all-inclusive luxury day trip to Morocco from Spain offering an opportunity to have a sightseeing tour around the city by visiting the Spartel Cape promontory, the pre-historic Caves of Hercules & experiencing the camel ride by the Atlantic shoreline.

description.text: The Tangier to Chefchaouen Day Trip is offered to allow you to enjoy what this uniquely blue city has to offer. You will have a nice drive through the spectacular and lush Rif Mountains while including stops for taking pictures.

Upon arrival at Chefchaouen , you will be amazed by its immense beauty being predominantly painted in blue to the extent it has acquired the title of “The Blue Pearl of Morocco”, the blue gradient is the prevalent factor here, from light to dark and every corner held another wondrous surprise of color and texture turning the town into a live museum of art. It is perched uphill at the feet of two mountains that have the shape of “goat’s horns” by which the town is named.

Your private driver will introduce you to your English- speaking private tour guide who has grown up within the walls of its Medina and has witnessed its recent transformation. Begin your tour by the Kasbah (fortress), which centers the Medina and its construction in 1471 to fight the Portuguese invasion from the Northern part of Morocco marks really the foundation of the city.

You will spend your time wandering around the shady blue streets and learning about the Moroccan and Andalusian Architecture while figuring out the actual history behind the blue color. Get to the waterfall, which is, in fact, a basin where women wash clothes and carpets, hanging them and waiting to dry with the sun. The view of the whole valley from here is amazing.

At this point, your choice of vouching for the day trip from Tangier to Chefchaouen has exceeded your expectations. From our experience, Chefchaouen has never failed to entice its guest visitors by the charm and attraction, which it has gained all this popularity worldwide.
After a nice time of strolling the Medina’s blue-painted alleyways, return back to the Uta El Hammam Square by the Kasbah for enjoying a delicious Moroccan lunch while watching the passers-by.

Continue your Tangier to Chefchaouen day trip through the peaceful shops that are exceptionally hassle-free and reasonably priced compared to other cities of Morocco, and then meet your driver again for a nice drive back to Tangier where you will be dropped off at the port to catch your ferry back to Spain or at the location of your choice in Tangier.
Please note that we also offer Short Trips from Tangier and Morocco Tours covering the best of this amazing destination.

This one day trip from Tarifa to Chefchaouen blends convenience, culture, and natural beauty. Your journey includes a scenic drive across northern Morocco, a guided walking tour of Chefchaouen, and enough free time to relax, shop, and take incredible photos of this picturesque town. Enjoy a comfortable one-hour ferry ride across the Strait of Gibraltar. Upon arrival, you’ll step onto African soil and be greeted by your private driver at the Tangier Ville port. He will be holding a welcome sign with your name.
08:15 A.M: DRIVE FROM TANGIER TO CHEFCHAOUEN
Hop into a private, air-conditioned vehicle for a scenic journey through the green hills and valleys of the Rif Mountains. Along the way, take in the changing landscapes and charming rural villages.
10:30 A.M.: ARRIVAL IN CHEFCHAOUEN & GUIDED TOUR

Reach Chefchaouen, the magical blue-washed town nestled in the Rif . Meet your local guide for a leisurely walking tour through the medina’s narrow streets, traditional markets, and hidden corners. Discover the kasbah, local artisan shops, and get an insider’s view of the town’s Andalusian and Berber heritage.

Meet your driver again and relax on the return drive through the Rif Mountains, heading back to the Tangier Ville port in time for your evening ferry.
Board the ferry back to Spain and reflect on your amazing Tarifa to Chefchaouen day trip as the sun sets over the sea. Arrive in Tarifa with a heart full of stories and photos worth sharing.

Passport & Border Control:

A valid passport is required for this day trip. Make sure it has at least 6 months of validity from the date of travel. There is passport control at both Tarifa and Tangier Ville ports, so allow time for border checks.
Ferry Schedule & Timing:

You will take the 8:00 a.m. ferry from Tarifa to Tangier and return on the 6:00 p.m. ferry back to Spain. Check-in at Tarifa port is required by 7:15 a.m. Ferry schedules may be subject to slight delays depending on weather and port traffic.
Currency in Morocco:

The local currency is the Moroccan Dirham (MAD). Many shops in Chefchaouen accept Euros, but it’s useful to have some local cash for small purchases. Your guide can help you find a money exchange office or ATM if needed.
Mobile Roaming & Wi-Fi:
Once in Morocco, you may enter roaming mode depending on your provider. It’s a good idea to activate international roaming or turn off data and use Wi-Fi when available to avoid unexpected charges.
Local Time Difference:
Morocco and Spain may be in different time zones depending on the season. Usually, Morocco is 1 hour behind Spain. We handle the coordination, but it’s good to be aware of the time difference.
Languages Spoken:
Your local guide in Chefchaouen speaks fluent English, Spanish, French, and Arabic. In Chefchaouen, people are friendly and often speak basic Spanish or French due to its Andalusian history.
Weather in Chefchaouen:
Chefchaouen enjoys a mild climate year-round. In summer, it’s warm and dry, while winter brings cooler temperatures, especially in the mountains. A light jacket is recommended in cooler months.
Photography Tips:

Chefchaouen is one of the most photogenic towns in Morocco. Bring your camera or smartphone fully charged—its blue-washed alleyways, colorful doors, and mountain backdrops make for stunning photos. Don’t forget to ask before photographing locals, especially in traditional areas.
Shopping & Souvenirs:

The medina is full of artisan shops selling handmade crafts, woven blankets, leather bags, natural soaps, and spices. Prices are usually negotiable, and your guide can help you get a fair deal if needed.

reviews.title: Overnight from Tarifa to Chefchaouen
reviews.text:
Omar was our excellent driver and tour guide. He picked us up once we arrived in Tangier from the ferry in a very nice full size Ford van. He drove us through areas of Tangier that you will not see on foot and then took us off to the mountains. He talked about the history of the area and stopped for us to take pictures multiple times.

Chefchaouen, the Blue City, was a feast for your eyes. We stayed near the top of the town at the Dar Lamar Guest House. Hamiz was a gracious host and served an excellent breakfast.

After an evening exploring on our own, including a Hammam and massage at the Luna Ryad and Spa (fabulous experience) we met our city tour guide, Foued, for a two hour walk around the town. Turns out not only is he a tour guide, but he is also a lawyer and budding photographer.

After the tour we had some time for lunch and to pick up some items at the local market before meeting Omar and driving back to Tangier for our ferry.

This overnight tour was a wonderful experience that we highly recommend. The tour operator was extremely responsive to all of our questions, literally within minutes of our What’s App message and the overall experience is unforgettable.

overview.text: Private Torremolinos to Morocco Day Trip

Looking for a unique escape from the Costa del Sol? Our private Torremolinos to Morocco day trip is the perfect opportunity to explore another continent in just one day. With hassle-free transportation, fast ferry tickets, and a guided tour in Tangier, this adventure offers a taste of Moroccan culture, history, and charm — all without the need for an overnight stay.

This all-inclusive day trip from Torremolinos to Morocco begins early in the morning and ends back at your hotel in the evening. You’ll cross the Strait of Gibraltar by ferry, meet your expert local guide in Tangier, and explore the city’s fascinating blend of Arab, Berber, and European influences. Whether it’s your first time in North Africa or a spontaneous add-on to your Spain vacation, this experience will stay with you forever.

description.text: Upon arrival at Tangier Ville port, you’ll be warmly welcomed by your private Moroccan guide holding a sign with your name. From there, begin your panoramic tour of Tangier. Drive past the Royal Palaces and Perdicaris Park, stop at Cape Spartel to enjoy stunning views where the Atlantic meets the Mediterranean, and take a short but memorable camel ride along the beach . Then, continue to the legendary Hercules Caves , an iconic symbol of Tangier’s mythology and history.

Delve into Tangier’s rich heritage with a walking tour through the Kasbah and Medina . Discover narrow alleyways, vibrant artisan markets, traditional shops, and local bakeries. Your guide will share insights into daily life, architecture, and local customs while you soak up the colors, sounds, and aromas of Morocco.

After a full day of exploration, your guide will accompany you back to the port. Board the ferry to Tarifa and meet your private driver waiting on the Spanish side. You’ll then be comfortably driven back to your hotel or address in Torremolinos, bringing your unforgettable day in Morocco to a close.

Our Torremolinos to Tangier day trip is ideal for travelers seeking adventure and cultural discovery in one unforgettable day. This all-inclusive tour covers round-trip transportation from Torremolinos, ferry tickets, a professional English-speaking guide in Morocco, and a rich itinerary that includes famous landmarks, local neighborhoods, and a camel ride by the Atlantic Ocean.

Is the tour suitable for children and seniors?
Yes, the Torremolinos to Tangier day trip is suitable for all ages. However, there is moderate walking in the Medina, so comfortable shoes and mobility should be considered.
Is the ferry crossing rough?
The ferry crossing is usually smooth and takes about 1 hour . However, in windy conditions, it may be choppy, motion sickness tablets are recommended for sensitive travelers.
Are ferry tickets and transportation included?
Yes, the round-trip ferry tickets and private transport from Torremolinos to Tarifa and back are all included in the tour.
Is there a vegetarian or vegan meal option?
Yes, vegetarian options are available , but please let us know at the time of booking so we can inform the restaurant in advance.
